children.translated_text: Oṃ. Salutation to <s>Viṣṇu</s>. Now in the <s>Khilas</s> (supplementary hymns), the purpose stated through the initial words of each <s>sūkta</s> (hymn): the characteristics of the presiding deities of the <s>Śatarcī</s> and others. (Khila I Introduction). The [metres are] <s>kṛti</s>, <s>prakṛti</s>, <s>ākṛti</s>, <s>vikṛti</s>, <s>saṃkṛti</s>, <s>abhikṛti</s>, <s>utkṛti</s>—thus eighty syllables.

A <s>tṛca</s> (three-verse group). 'Eternally'—six less [than the full]. <s>Tārkṣya Suparṇa</s>. The <s>Āśvina</s> [hymn]. That seventh [verse] is to <s>Agni</s>; the distant one to <s>Indra</s>; the eleventh—or the ninth—the deity is indicated by the mark. From the eighth onward, four are in <s>Virāj</s> form. In <s>Jagatī</s> metre. The chest [section] in <s>Bṛhatī</s>. Seven [verses] are <s>Brāhmya</s>.
Having looked upward with the supreme <s>Āditya</s> (Sun), with mighty radiance,
I take upon myself the glory of the glorious ones, all forms.
Rising today, share with us, as a father to his sons.
You are the lord of long life; grant us that, O <s>Sūrya</s>.
You who are rising, O great friend, ascending, O far-seeing one,
may we see a hundred autumns, may we live a hundred autumns.
I urge that much-invoked <s>Meṣa</s>, praised in hymns. ||1
Eternally, O <s>Nāsatyas</s>, the cows praise your greatness, abundant in gifts, always.
When you, O <s>Aśvins</s>, carried <s>Bhujyu</s> home, <s>Tugra's</s> [son], on the supportless path, to [his] home.
When the white horse, striking, O <s>Nāsatyas</s>, [you rescued] <s>Bhujyu</s>, for the well-being of <s>Perava</s>.
That delight—the inspired sages, praising at assemblies, went to the mind-captivating <s>Dasras</s> (Aśvins).
Come to our pressing, O you two praiseworthy ones; may well-yoked swans carry you.
You both, like young men, the praises—desiring you, O <s>Dasras</s>, O bulls, they accompany.
Come to us with the threefold [libation]; the <s>Soma</s> is for drinking; come with your chariot, O celestial ones, to the pressing for exhilaration.
The <s>barhis</s> (sacred grass) is spread for you; the sweet [offerings] are well-pressed; the priests are yoked, charioteers, skilled of hand.
O <s>Vāsatyas</s> (Aśvins), wonderful ones, the treasure of the world, O Heaven and Earth, listen to me, O two worlds.
May those <s>Aśvins</s>, whose steeds are donkeys, [come to] my invocation, O lords of beauty, come together with <s>Sūryā</s>. ||2
May streams of honey and ghee flow forth; may the mighty ones press the potent <s>Soma</s>.
Thus, O young <s>Aśvins</s>, may the two arms yield nourishment with honey and ghee.
O <s>Agni</s>, may the attendants rejoice; the praises go forth to heaven, to the hot [offering].
The fourteenth, the third heaven, the young one—may he measure out strength and wealth, O <s>Sumeka</s>.
I urge the tawny drop, the much-praised bull, victorious.
The one with tawny horses, seven tawny steeds yoked, the wheel-rim with three naves—[praises] to <s>Varuṇa</s> for well-being.
<s>Soma</s> [with] <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> greatness and power—the seven sages, heroic men, gladden [him].
The sons of <s>Sudhanvan</s>, skilled of hand, with <s>Śamī</s> sticks—<s>Tvaṣṭar</s>, <s>Āṅgirasa</s>, <s>Ṛbhu</s>—for well-being.
Here, here, O bounteous one, I place for you the firm and potent <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, who delights the heart.
I bestow wealth upon the offerer of <s>havis</s> (oblation); even the heated <s>gharma</s> (hot milk offering), they carry forth. ||3
Eternally the two eagles, [the hymn] woven strand by strand, all-consuming, path-guarding, men-watching.
This crow, cherishing, awakened me from sleep, while the questioners were cherishing.
That single-rimmed, triple-layered, sixteen-spoked, hundred-walled [wheel], with twenty counter-spokes,
with eight [and] six divisions, of all forms, with a single noose, of three paths, two marks, and one delusion.
Always, always, one by one, standing—thirty-five and ten more.
Thirty, auspicious, nine, the secret sacrifice, sixty-eight he found.
He mounted the mighty thunderbolt, the heroic one, holding fast, the god, the tawny-haired <s>Indra</s>.
May this <s>Indra</s>, the sixteenth, grant protection; six armored ones, one firm—together. ||4
May streams of honey and ghee flow forth, that you found in the cow <s>Sūri</s>.
<s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>, fashioners of the world—may the <s>Aśvins</s> enjoy my pressings.
The comfortable chariot, going a hundred leagues, swift, the morning-going, easy-seated, golden one—
wherein the daughter of <s>Vivasvat</s> mounted—that very [chariot] we call hither for our aid.
Your horses, yoked to the chariot, wise, swift as the wind, dripping with ghee—
with those, just as [you went] to <s>Sūryā</s>, O <s>Dasras</s>, increase us in battles.
Whatever nourishing seed, O <s>Aśvins</s>, whatever the donkey [gave] to <s>Vadhrimatī</s>, O generous ones,
from which was born one dear to the gods, skilled—give that to her, O healers, O day-born ones.
Whatever medicine, O <s>Nāsatyas</s>, O brilliant ones, by which you helped <s>Ghoṣā</s>, desirous of offspring,
give that to her, the bride among three men, by which she may find a husband, she of beautiful hands.
<s>Vaṣaṭ</s> to you, O <s>Dasras</s>, at this pressing, O <s>Nāsatyas</s>—may the priest make [the offering], the wise one.
May the woman who has rightly conceived give birth easily; may her joints open for delivery.
Thus, sitting down and sitting near, O inspired ones, the two well-yoked eagles praising you,
the prayer, the rite, powerful at assemblies—bestow upon those two a son, a foremost offspring. ||5
The luminous, radiant, three-wheeled, comfortable chariot, easy-seated, of many wonders—
of brilliant gifts, at whose yoking [all] was born—that [chariot] I invoke for you two to drink the surplus.
You two gods, with ancient wisdom, yoked to the chariot, mighty, worthy of worship—
come, O <s>Nāsatyas</s>, with your powers; drink this third pressing.
You two gods, thirty-three, and the eleven—the true ones have placed the truth foremost.
Enjoying our sacrifice and pressing, drink the <s>Soma</s>, O <s>Aśvins</s>, O bright-fired ones.
Worthy of praise is that deed of yours, O <s>Aśvins</s>—the bull of heaven, of the atmosphere, of the earth.
A thousand praises, and those [praises] for cattle—come to all of that to drink.
This share is deposited for you, O worshipful ones—come to these songs, O <s>Nāsatyas</s>.
Drinking the honey-sweet <s>Soma</s>, O <s>Aśvins</s>, protect the generous worshipper with your powers. ||6
Luminous, fair-faced, with unceasing radiance, O bright-fired ones.
Make auspiciousness for all creatures; do not harm person or being.
<s>Dhātar</s>, <s>Rāti</s>, <s>Savitar</s>—may they enjoy this; <s>Tvaṣṭar</s>, who became the messenger of <s>Vivasvat</s>.
Together with the <s>Aśvins</s> and <s>Uṣas</s> (Dawn), that wide, cow-rich [wealth]—great, O singer, O <s>Indra</s>.
O youngest <s>Agni</s>, of <s>Bharadvāja</s> who presses [Soma], come; the most honey-rich pressed [Soma is ready].
Of <s>Soma's</s> power, contemplating me, having generated the vessel, it came to aid from the depths.
<s>Agni</s>, broad, <s>Brahmaṇaspati</s>, <s>Soma</s>—he stretched forth among the gods.
The lordship of <s>Indra</s> [is mine]; O <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, [accept] my oblations.
Generating the <s>Brāhmī</s> splendor, the gods at the beginning said:
'He who, a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, would know this—the gods would be under his control.' ||7
O lord of the world, though lean, you protect—wondrous among the gods.
O <s>Aśvins</s>, protect us who seek you, O <s>Nāsatyas</s>, throughout the day.
O <s>Suparṇa</s> (eagle), bring that one here; the sons of heaven have sat down.
<s>Agni</s> became <s>Jātavedas</s> (knower of all beings) of creatures, the all-seeing one.
<s>Agni</s>, the priest, resplendent, wealthy—the highest glory of the gods.
Again, <s>Agni</s>, <s>Prajāpati</s>, <s>Vaiśvānara</s> (universal fire), the golden one.
May <s>Agni</s> be the protector, the auspicious one, the sheltering one, of all the gods.
Protect [our] wealth from all sides, O <s>Soma</s>-drinker; create fearlessness.
O <s>Agni</s>, strike down the vital spots of the enemies and of the niggardly.
You are the lord of long life; grant us that, O <s>Sūrya</s>.
You who are rising, O great friend, ascending, O far-seeing one,
may we see a hundred autumns, may we live a hundred autumns. ||8
The lean, blind sage <s>Cyavana</s>, grown old, O <s>Aśvins</s>—you made [him whole] with your acts.
Making him sighted, of robust body, mighty—again a young man, a husband indeed of maidens.
Whoever [worships] you with <s>Soma</s> offerings, with oblations, with ghee, with the <s>Veda</s>, with mind—O powerful ones,
he obtains brilliant, <s>Indra</s>-accompanied treasure, much desired, conquering in battle, rich in heroes.
<s>Saptavadhri</s>, the sage, sends forth to you a hymn with [his] thought, a song to you two, now.
The trees [were his] ocean—O <s>Uśanas</s>, the young one—then make him free from harm.
<s>Saptavadhri</s> cried out, skilled of hand, bound to a tree, a noble kinsman, the humped one.
You two split open his tree, like a thunderbolt-wielding [Indra breaks] a rock, mightily raining.
The lone, lean, desiring one — [O helpers], the generous hero.
The prayer was made for your increase—bestow upon him always the destruction of enemies. ||9
These are your allotted shares, O <s>Indra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>, flowing forth at the great pressings for you.
At every sacrifice, you eagerly [attend] the pressings; you assist the one who presses and sacrifices.
The flowing herbs and waters—through you two, O <s>Indra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>, [they] have attained greatness.
[Those waters] that stood beyond the boundary of the atmosphere—no enemy has ever assailed [those] of you two.
Truly, O <s>Indra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>, dripping with ghee, the seven voices milk out a wave of honey.
With those, O lords of beauty, protect the generous worshipper who, undeceived, guards the cow with his thoughts.
Dripping with ghee, belonging to <s>Soma</s>, swift, nourishing—the seven sisters, the seat of <s>Ṛta</s> (cosmic order).
Those of yours, O <s>Indra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>, dripping with ghee—with those, bestow skill upon the sacrificer.
We have spoken for great good fortune; truly, to you two mighty ones, [we declare] the <s>Indriya</s> (Indra-like) greatness.
O <s>Indra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>, dripping with ghee, protect us with thrice seven [aids], O lords of beauty.
O <s>Indra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>, whatever thought, speech, and heard [wisdom] the sages placed in the mind at the beginning,
those metres the wise ones created, seeing the sacrifice as they extended it through <s>tapas</s> (austerity).
O <s>Indra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>, bestow upon the sacrificers undistorted good will and increase of wealth.
Bestow upon us progeny, prosperity, wealth; extend our lifespan for long life. ||10
This <s>Soma</s>, well-prepared, pressed by stones, purified by prayers, praised in <s>ukthas</s> (hymns),
mixed with milk, exhilarating, sung with <s>Sāman</s> chants—come quickly around the mountain, O fair-lipped ones.
Drink of this pressed juice, [its] splendor—the foremost purified [offerings], O bulls.
O <s>Aśvins</s>, fill your bellies; then set your minds to bestowing wealth.
Come here, eager in body; the sweet [offerings] desiring us—with wisdom.
The delightful [praise], much-trembling, youthful, calls you two with its thought.
O <s>Nāsatyas</s>, mount the comfortable chariot with rays, the pleasant, well-conveying one, you two.
Whom the tawny mares, the swiftest carriers, convey for you two — a hundred horses, or seven divine ones,
whom pursuing, come you two, being praised, to the dwelling of <s>Śāryāta</s>, descendant of <s>Manu</s>,
fearless, delighting in the communal feast — <s>Cyavana</s> [brought] the gods; he is that one [devoted] to you two.
O <s>Aśvins</s>, with your threefold chariot, bring hither wealth accompanied by brave heroes.
Hearing, I invoke you two for protection; be for our growth and in the winning of prizes. [11]
When you two yoke the bounteous swift [horse], much desired, valiant in battle, rich in heroes,
your own chariot, O wondrous ones (<s>Dasrā</s>), in the invocations — then it goes forth along the courses of [your] forms.
Most joyful, these sages move about; like the <s>Turvaśas</s> bound together in contests,
impelling speech that is richly adorned, with oblations, to give delight at the pressing.
Having heard [our] call, satisfy the worshipper; [fulfill] the desire of these; bring the oblations.
And protect the praisers and the sacrificer with your aids, O two lords of men, in the encounter. [12]
To whomever you two go — the <s>soma</s>-presser, the god-accompanied one — the oblation-maker, you two bulls, to whom the offering is given,
he prospers with food a hundredfold, openly, with hymns, the generous one, drinking the prepared [<s>soma</s>], the giver.
Whatever wondrous deeds of yours, hard to surpass, the singers praise at the <s>soma</s>-pressings,
may they prosper here through your bounties among the people — you who partake of <s>soma</s>-drinking at the assembly.
When you two, willing bulls, fitted back the head of <s>Dadhyañc</s>, O healers,
that [head], O youthful ones, honeysweet, with consecrated offering — you two enjoy it, delighting.
O <s>Ātharvaṇa</s>, speak not what I tell you: your honey is unthought of by other, mightier ones.
What the bounteous one commanded <s>Dadhyañc</s> — that he proclaimed to you through the horse's head.
When the mace-armed one came to attack, <s>Dadhyañc</s> gives honey to the fathers for us.
'Do not say this to the ill-woven one' — when she spoke, that was your fair renown.
With which powers you [aided] <s>Dadhyañc</s>, O bulls, with which <s>Tura Kāvaśeya</s> in the sacrifice,
with which you inspire thought at the deep watering-place — with those protect us at the assembly. [13]
This <s>soma</s>, devoted to the gods, O wise ones, heart-touching, goes to the inspired ones, exchanging.
Sweetest of oblations, more than honey or ghee — a new hymn to you, O <s>Aśvins</s>, I offer.
The great [inspiration] delights your divine desire, through which you have crossed all the ways.
May you two <s>Aśvins</s>, of manifold enjoyment, well-praised, sages-befriending, grant the all-nourishing [cow].
He who is rich in cattle, rich in horses, generous in speech, of many splendors, desiring what is coveted,
whom I invoke when the charioteer seeks cattle — him I call to the chariot of all forms.
Your chariot, O bulls, with good wheels, a good carrier, much desired, wealth-finding, life-sustaining,
with which you bring prizes accompanied by coveted heroes, with broad glory, and nourishing, and honey-sweet horses. [14]
This, O gods, is the ancient portion which the exultant sacrificial ones have taken.
This is his <s>gharma</s> (hot milk offering), purified by <s>ṛc</s>-verses; that you drink, O charioteers, running forth.
When the head of <s>Makha</s> was cut off, O bulls, you healers fitted it back.
That body of yours, beautiful and splendid, the sages always praise at the <s>soma</s>-pressings.
With which the gods struck down the demons, with which they overcame the godless armies,
with which they became immortal, O <s>soma</s>-holders — that [head] you fitted with the horse's head.
Formerly, scattered by the ceremony, the gods reached neither a remnant nor heaven.
Having sacrificed for many years, when his head was given, having fitted it, they ascended to heaven. [15]
When your mother approached the fierce ones, the well-wheeled chariots, unwavering, <s>Saraṇyū</s>,
there for you two, O <s>Aśvins</s>, the honey-sweet, set with honey, the ancient well-guided blessing.
You two with hymns raise up to heaven; you two place nourishments in the <s>Śakvarī</s> [verses].
You two with plants release this great [one]; you two release the rivers for flowing.
You two, honey-sweet, with sweet honeyed [gifts]; you two are healers, O good-handed physicians.
You two on chariots, with charioteers, are mighty, auspicious, with those that drive away disease.
Grant me that eye-sight of my eyes to see clearly; may we behold the sun and these directions.
By which, looking forth, we may overpower <s>Śakra</s> — hard-pressed by you two <s>Aśvins</s>, O heroes, in the winning of prizes. [16]
O <s>Aśvins</s>, bring rich [offerings], with <s>svadhā</s> and horses, the wives of <s>Dāsa</s>, with waters.
Your gifts are like <s>Āditya</s> in heaven; your nourishments shine forth, most radiant.
When <s>Rebha</s>, O wondrous ones, was hidden in the waters, striving for youth, striving for strength, from the pit,
you raised him up, O <s>Aśvins</s>, and the maimed swift one — that vow of yours the hymn-reciters magnify.
Those [aids] of yours that are in the body, that are on earth, that are in plants, in stones, in the atmosphere,
that are among heroes, among patrons, and in heaven — with those grant us shelter, a hundredfold, O youthful ones.
He who with [your] support brings the gifts of the praiser — the oblations that propitiate, that overpower enemies,
that protect, that continuously bestow [blessings] — with those grant us shelter, a hundredfold, O youthful ones. [17]
Your three-wheeled, well-seated, well-resting chariot, with three seats, bearing a banner, swift as the wind,
at whose yoking the radiant [dawn] extends the rein — where you two sit, granting delight.
You two carried <s>Vimada</s>'s bride; you two made the cow a milch-cow for <s>Śayu</s>.
You two with life extended beyond bondage — you freed <s>Atri</s> from distress.
A father offered his sheep for the she-wolf's kindness; he made the seer blind, O <s>Aśvins</s>.
On that tawny horse you placed eyes; you revealed his world again.
That eye of yours in heaven, O divine eagle, with which you two immortals behold the worlds,
grant those [two] eyes to me, O divine kinsmen — worshipping, may you find us, who are devoted. Approaching the sacrifice. [18]
Adhyāya II (Khila, II <s>Anukramaṇī</s>).

[<s>Anukramaṇī</s> index:] One [verse] 'mā' [beginning], 'bhadram' five <s>anuṣṭubh</s> [verses], 'jāgarṣi' one to <s>Jātavedas</s>, 'svastyayanam' two, 'varṣantu' one, 'hiraṇyavarṇām' one less than [a full set] — <s>Śrī Bhārgavī</s>, the dispeller of <s>Alakṣmī</s>, <s>Śrī</s>, in <s>anuṣṭubh</s> meter ending with <s>śakvarī</s>, the fourth <s>hiṃsā</s> to <s>Agni</s>, <s>prastārapaṅkti</s>, <s>triṣṭubh</s> the fifteenth and beyond <s>bṛhatī</s>, <s>Śrī</s>'s sons the latter six, 'ciklītaḥ' five, <s>Ānanda</s> and <s>Kardama</s>, <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>, 'mayi śleṣaś' <s>śleṣa</s> to <s>Jātavedas</s>, <s>bṛhatī</s> etc., 'saṃsravantu' about streams, <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>, the second onwards <s>triṣṭubh</s>, 'ā te' seven, for progeny, embryo-purpose, blessing-praise, <s>Prajāpati</s>, <s>Aindravāyavya</s>, fourth <s>bṛhatī</s>, fifth <s>prastārapaṅkti</s> — 'agniḥ' five, for living sons, <s>Agni-Vāruṇa</s>, <s>atijagatī</s>, <s>ānuṣṭup</s>, ending with <s>triṣṭubh</s>, 'cakṣur' one, self-praise, 'śaṃvatī' six, <s>śānti</s> (peace), <s>ānuṣṭubh</s>, from the fifth <s>bṛhatī</s> and <s>jagatī</s>, 'svapna' one, 'yasya upa' <s>anuṣṭubh</s>, the <s>Vālakhilyas</s>, the remaining eight.
Fear not! You shall not die. I protect you all around.
With a club I slay the scorpion, and the serpent that has come, with a staff.
You, O <s>Agni</s>, by days, you the swiftly blazing one. [1]
With the speed of the sun's chariot and the strength of <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s arm,
with the swooping of <s>Garuḍa</s>'s wings, go to the ground, O greatly renowned one!
At the very birth of <s>Garuḍa</s>, the three worlds trembled.
The whole earth trembled, with its mountains, forests, and groves.
The sky, with sun and moon vanished, and the stars do not shine.
The deities, seized with fear — the wind does not blow, the wind does not blow. Oṃ namaḥ.
O serpent, auspicious one, blessings to you! Go far away, O greatly renowned one!
Remember the words of <s>Āstīka</s> at the end of <s>Janamejaya</s>'s sacrifice.
The serpent who, having heard the words of <s>Āstīka</s>, does not turn back,
his head shall be split into a hundred pieces, like the fruit of the <s>śiṃśapā</s> tree.
<s>Agastya</s> and <s>Mādhava</s>, <s>Mucukunda</s> the great sage,
<s>Kapila</s> the sage, and <s>Āstīka</s> — these five are sleepers of ease.
Salutation to <s>Narmadā</s> in the morning, salutation to <s>Narmadā</s> at night.
Homage to you, O <s>Narmadā</s>; protect me from the venomous serpent.
He who was born of <s>Jaratkāru</s>, the greatly renowned, to <s>Jaratkāru</s> the maiden,
by that one's [power], O serpent, blessings to you! Go far away, O greatly renowned one!
The serpent-nature of that serpent — to that serpent, homage to you.
Speak auspiciously from the south, speak auspiciously from the north,
speak auspiciously before us, speak auspiciously behind, O <s>Kapiñjala</s> bird!
Speak auspiciously regarding sons, speak auspiciously regarding the household,
speak auspiciously for us, speak auspiciously for our safety,
speak auspiciously below us, speak auspiciously above us,
speak auspiciously, auspiciously to us, speak auspiciously all around us.
May there be no rival before us; make it auspicious to the south;
may there always be fearlessness behind; may there be good fortune to the north, in the home.
You magnify youthful vigor, like a drum for those who seek victory.
O <s>Śakuntaka</s> bird, circling, with a hundred wings, speak to us!
Speaking, O bird, speak auspiciously, speak auspiciously! [2]
You are awake, O <s>Jātavedas</s>, in the world; you are awake where the oblation-possessor sacrifices.
I offer this oblation with faith; with it, protect the secret name of the cows.
Knowing, releasing [the cows] from heaven, splitting the rock with hymns. [3]
The auspicious one, <s>Tārkṣya</s>, with unbroken rim, the great being, the eagle-bird of the gods,
the demon-slayer, <s>Indra</s>'s companion in battles, the greatly renowned — may we mount as upon a ship.
The distress-releasing one of the <s>Aṅgirases</s>, <s>Gaya</s>, the auspicious one of <s>Atri</s>, and <s>Tārkṣya</s> in mind.
With joined hands I take refuge; may there be well-being for us in difficulties, may there be fearlessness. [4]
Forth, O <s>Śyāvāśva</s>, boldly!
May they rain, O radiant ones, the lightnings of heaven's cloud.
May all seeds sprout; strike down the hater of sacred knowledge.
To the sovereign, with great verse, deep. [5]
She who is golden-colored, beautiful, adorned with a garland of gold and silver,
the moon-like, golden <s>Lakṣmī</s> — bring her to me, O <s>Jātavedas</s>.
Bring to me, O <s>Jātavedas</s>, that <s>Lakṣmī</s> who never departs,
by whom I may find gold, cattle, horses, and servants.
With horses in front, a chariot in the middle, rejoicing at the trumpeting of elephants,
I invoke the goddess <s>Śrī</s>; may the goddess <s>Śrī</s> be pleased with me.
I desire her, golden-cloaked, moist, blazing, satiated, and satiating,
standing on a lotus, lotus-colored — I invoke <s>Śrī</s> here.
The radiant one, the luminous, blazing with glory, <s>Śrī</s> cherished by the gods in the world, the noble one,
I take refuge in that lotus-rimmed one; may <s>Alakṣmī</s> (misfortune) perish from me — I choose you. [6]
O one of the sun's color, born from your austerity, the tree — your tree is the <s>bilva</s>,
may its fruits, through austerity, drive away inner illusions and external misfortune.
May the companion of the gods approach me, along with fame and the jewel.
I have manifested in this realm; may he grant me fame and prosperity.
Hunger, thirst, impurity — I destroy the eldest <s>Alakṣmī</s> (misfortune).
Destitution and failure — drive away all of them from my house.
She who is accessible through fragrance, irresistible, ever nourished, rich in cow-dung [fuel],
I invoke here <s>Śrī</s> (prosperity), the sovereign of all beings.
May we attain the desire of the mind, the purpose, and the truth of speech.
May the form of cattle, of food—may <s>Śrī</s> and glory rest in me.
O <s>Kardama</s>, [you who are] born as offspring, be manifest in me, O <s>Kardama</s>.
Establish <s>Śrī</s>, the mother adorned with lotuses, in my family.
May the waters flow unctuous; O <s>Ciklīta</s>, dwell in my house.
And establish the divine mother <s>Śrī</s> in my house.
[She who is] ripened, lotus-adorned, nourished, tawny, wearing a lotus garland,
O <s>Jātavedas</s>, bring to me <s>Lakṣmī</s>—radiant like the sun, golden.
[She who is] moist, lotus-adorned, of stately form, golden, wearing a gold garland,
O <s>Jātavedas</s>, bring to me <s>Lakṣmī</s>—radiant like the moon, golden.
O <s>Jātavedas</s>, bring to me that <s>Lakṣmī</s>, the unfailing one,
From whom I may find abundant gold, cattle, female servants, and men. || 8 ||
He who entered into bliss ran toward <s>Vibhāvasu</s> (fire).
May all the <s>Śrī</s>s attend upon [him]; O <s>Ciklīta</s>, dwell in my house.
O <s>Kardama</s>, creator of offspring, let us attain prosperity.
He bestowed and approached; we have released the desires of those [who came].
O <s>Jātavedas</s>, purify me and bestow abundance of wealth.
May <s>Agni</s> release me from all sin and distress.
O <s>Agni</s>, friend and mighty one, announce to the gods the good will of the two worlds (heaven and earth).
Grant well-being, good dwelling, [and blessings] from heaven to men. May we cross over hatreds, distresses, and difficulties—may we cross over, may we cross over by your aid. || 9 ||
He who, having become pure and devoted, offers <s>ājya</s> (clarified butter) daily,
And constantly recites the fifteen-verse <s>sūkta</s> (hymn), desiring <s>Śrī</s> (prosperity),
O lotus-faced one, lotus-thighed one, lotus-eyed one, born of the lotus,
O lotus-eyed one, grant me that by which I may obtain happiness.
O giver of horses, giver of cattle, giver of wealth, O great wealth!
May wealth delight me, O goddess; grant me all desires.
Sons, grandsons, wealth, grain, elephants, horses, and other [animals], cattle, chariots—
You are the mother of all beings; grant me long life.
Wealth is <s>Agni</s>, wealth is <s>Vāyu</s>, wealth is <s>Sūrya</s>, wealth is <s>Vasu</s>.
Wealth is <s>Indra</s> and <s>Bṛhaspati</s>; I offer up to <s>Varuṇa</s> as wealth.
O <s>Vainateya</s>, drink the <s>Soma</s>; may <s>Vṛtrahā</s> (slayer of <s>Vṛtra</s>) drink the <s>Soma</s>.
May the possessors of <s>Soma</s> give me the <s>Soma</s> of wealth.
Neither anger nor envy, neither greed nor inauspicious thoughts
arise in those of meritorious deeds; the devoted ones should recite the <s>Śrī Sūkta</s>.
O you who dwell in the lotus lake, with lotus in hand, more resplendent than white, beautiful with auspicious garlands and fragrance,
O <s>Bhagavatī</s>, beloved of <s>Hari</s>, enchanting one, bestower of prosperity upon the three worlds—be gracious to me.
May [this hymn] bestow splendor, longevity, health, auspiciousness, and great fame.
Grain, wealth, cattle, abundant gain of sons, and a long life of a hundred years.
The consort of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the forbearing goddess, <s>Mādhavī</s>, dear to <s>Mādhava</s>,
<s>Lakṣmī</s>, dear companion of the gods—I bow to the beloved of <s>Acyuta</s>.
We know <s>Mahālakṣmī</s>; we meditate on the consort of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
May that <s>Lakṣmī</s> inspire us.
O lotus-faced one, O <s>Padminī</s>, with lotus-petal [eyes], O lotus-lover, with eyes extending like lotus petals,
O beloved of the universe, favorable to the mind of the universe—place your lotus feet in my heart.
<s>Ānanda</s>, <s>Kardama</s>, <s>Śrīta</s>, and <s>Ciklīta</s> [are] spread about.
The seers are the sons of <s>Śrī</s>; and <s>Śrī</s> the goddess is the deity of the gods.
May debts, diseases, and poverty, sin, hunger, and untimely death,
fear, grief, and mental anguish be destroyed for me always.
Moon-bright <s>Lakṣmī</s>, sovereign <s>Śrī</s>, sun-bright, imperial,
Radiant with the hues of the moon, sun, and fire—we worship <s>Mahālakṣmī</s>.
May the lightning-bearing clouds of heaven rain down upon you, O shining one.
May all seeds sprout; strike down the foe of <s>Brahman</s>.
O lotus-lover, O <s>Padminī</s>, lotus-handed, lotus-faced,
O beloved of the universe, favorable to <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s mind—place your lotus feet upon me.
She who sits upon the lotus, with broad hips, with eyes extending like lotus petals, deep,
with a rounded navel, bent by the weight of her breasts, with a bright white upper garment,
<s>Lakṣmī</s>, bathed by divine lordly elephants with golden jars studded with clusters of gems,
may she, always lotus-handed, dwell in my house, endowed with all auspiciousness.
<s>Siddha-Lakṣmī</s>, <s>Mokṣa-Lakṣmī</s>, <s>Jaya-Lakṣmī</s>, <s>Sarasvatī</s>,
<s>Śrī-Lakṣmī</s>, <s>Vara-Lakṣmī</s>—may they be gracious to me always.
Bearing in her hands a boon, <s>kuśa</s> grass, a noose, and [the gesture of] fearlessness, seated on a lotus,
Radiant as a million rising suns, three-eyed—I worship that primordial sovereign of the universe.
O most auspicious of all auspicious things, O <s>Śivā</s>, accomplisher of all aims,
O refuge, O three-eyed <s>Gaurī</s>, O <s>Nārāyaṇī</s>—salutations to you.
<s>Ciklīta</s>, whose name is such, day and night, O wise one,
Shine upon us for union and for life. O <s>Jātavedas</s>, may the divine people purify me.
May they purify with the mind and with thoughts; may all beings purify.
O <s>Jātavedas</s>, what has been praised by us—
O <s>Viśvedevas</s> (all-gods), purify me. O <s>Jātavedas</s>, purify me.
Those born among us, heroes, stand firm among the firm.
Firm is the sky, firm is the earth, the firm stands firm among the firm.
O <s>Agni</s>, what has been praised—bestow abundance of wealth.
O <s>Agni</s>, friend and mighty one, announce to the gods the good will of the two worlds.
Grant well-being, good dwelling, [and blessings] from heaven to men. May we cross over hatreds, distresses, and difficulties—may we cross over, may we cross over by your aid. || 10 ||
May [prosperity] cling to me; do not harm [me]. [Grant] sovereignty and prosperity, O wise one.
Fill us for union and for life. O <s>Jātavedas</s>, purify me.
The mortal who would assail us—may he not overcome [us], like one mounted on a chariot.
O <s>Vibhāvasu</s> (fire), [destroy] those who attack; and [grant] your wakefulness and wisdom.
May the cows be free from disease; may the pregnant one deliver safely.
Whatever enemies there are, and heroes, with their forces—
Bestow abundance of wealth. O <s>Jātavedas</s>, purify me.
May our cows be the dawns, many in the pen, dripping with ghee.
O <s>Agni</s>, friend and mighty one, announce to the gods the good will of the two worlds.
Grant well-being, good dwelling, [and blessings] from heaven to men. May we cross over hatreds, distresses, and difficulties—may we cross over, may we cross over by your aid. || 11 ||
May the <s>Maruts</s> stream together, and the horses, and the men.
May the abundance of grain stream together; with the streaming oblation I offer.
Let the cattle come here, those that have wandered away, whose companion <s>Vāyu</s> has delighted in.
<s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> who knows their forms—may <s>Savitṛ</s> protect them in this world.
Let the cattle stream together to this pen; may <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, knowing, bring them.
May <s>Sinīvālī</s> lead them at the front; as they have come, O <s>Anumatī</s>, restrain them.
I sprinkle the milk of the cows together with ghee, strength, and sap.
Our heroes are sprinkled; may the cows stand firm for the lord of cattle.
I bring the milk of the cows; I bring grain and sap.
Our heroes are brought; [I bring] the wives—this is the eighth. || 12 ||
May your embryo enter the womb, a male, like an arrow into a quiver.
May a hero be born here, a son, after ten months.
I perform for you the <s>Prājāpatya</s> rite; may the embryo enter your womb,
undiminished, complete; may it be born not blind, not lame, not afflicted by demons.
May a male son be born to you; may a male be born after.
The auspicious seeds that the bulls beget for us—
may those auspicious seeds the bulls beget for you.
By them may you bear a son; may he be born the most heroic of his kin.
The embryo that is in the barren cow, and [the bull] that impregnates—<s>Indra</s> placed that in the tree.
By them may you find sons; be a fruitful milch-cow.
May your minds know each other; may your navels [unite]; may there be [harmony] from that.
I yoke you with the bond of desire, for the sake of non-separation.
May desire be fulfilled for me, ever unconquered.
Whatever desire I desire, O <s>Vāyu</s>, fulfill it for me. || 13 ||
May <s>Agni</s> come first among the gods; may he release the offspring of this [woman] from the noose of death.
May king <s>Varuṇa</s> approve of this, so that this woman may not weep for [the death of] a grandson.
May this <s>Agni Gārhaspatya</s> (household fire) protect her; may he extend long life for her offspring.
May this [woman] with a non-empty lap live as a mother; may she awaken to the joy of a grandson.
May no fearful [sound] arise in your house at night; let those who cry enter elsewhere, not near you.
Do not stand with disheveled hair, beating your breast; living with sons, shine forth in the world of your husband, seeing your progeny with a joyful mind.
The sin of childlessness, the death of a grandchild, and evil or guilt—
I release you from these as from offspring [bonds]; I release the bonds toward the enemies.
The <s>brāhmaṇa</s> rite fashioned by the gods—by that I strike down the demons dwelling in the womb.
I cast down the flesh-eating deaths; may your sons live long lives.
For you, O <s>Agni</s>, are the first protector. || 14 ||
The eye and the ear, the mind and speech, <s>prāṇa</s> (inbreath) and <s>apāna</s> (outbreath)—this is the body.
Two [channels] going inward, two going outward, and the two excretory [passages]—I consider this the tenfold mechanism, the fountain.
[He] who brought [them] from afar. || 15 ||
The chest and the back, the hands and the arms, the shanks and the thighs, the belly and the head,
hair, flesh, blood, bones, marrow—this body is like a water-bubble.
The eyebrows and the forehead, and also the ears, the jaws, the cheeks, and the chin,
the lips and the teeth, and likewise the tongue—this body of mine is a jewel-case of the face.
The auspicious ones recite this; ask the speech as it is.
Having approached the agreed-upon assembly—whoever says 'this is it.'
The wife, the assembly, the <s>parisrut</s> (filtered liquor); <s>Bhāratī</s>, speaker of <s>Brahman</s>,
The great [earth], knowing, was born—whoever says 'this is it.'
<s>Indra</s>—what [is he]? The mighty, the powerful lord. With radiance he makes offering.
By that he illuminated the sun, by which [he sustains] these two worlds.
O <s>Agni</s>, enjoy [the offering of] <s>Aṅgiras</s> <s>Kāṇva</s> <s>Medhyātithi</s>.
May the most sweet-tasting [<s>Soma</s>] of the pressed juice not overpower you, O <s>Soma</s>.
O <s>Agni</s> of the <s>Aṅgiras</s>es, blaze forth, most inviting to the gods.
O most beneficent one, with the most beneficent hymns, they made peace and well-being.
May the roaring god <s>Parjanya</s> rain upon us; may the plants flourish.
May heaven and earth be auspicious for us, auspicious for our offspring; may it be well for bipeds, well for quadrupeds.
May <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s> be favorable to us with their aid. || 16 ||
O sleep, in the abode of sleep, put all people to sleep.
Put the others to sleep until sunrise; may I alone remain awake.
Who are those men, manifested, sharing the same nest? || 17 ||
The serpent named <s>Ajagara</s>, the great serpent without venom,
in him a serpent is well-placed; by that we put you to sleep.
A serpent, a snake, <s>Ajagara</s>, the great one without venom,
from that serpent [come] the rivers; we have found their depth.
The serpent named <s>Kālika</s>, with the strength of nine thousand <s>Nāgas</s>,
born in the pool of the <s>Yamunā</s>, who is the vehicle of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>,
whether [there be] fear from the messenger of <s>Kālika</s>, or from <s>Kālika</s> [himself]—
Having crossed beyond the birthplace, the <s>Kālika</s> (serpent) goes forth without poison. (p.86)
Come, O <s>Indra</s>, by the invoked paths; enjoy this our sacrificial share.
Like the wife of a maternal uncle who has been satisfied — your share, O paternal cousin, is like the omentum.
Fame-bringing, powerful, sovereign — that very one became the king, the overlord.
Lord of mingled elephants, horses, and men — perpetual auspiciousness, long life.
<s>Karkoṭaka</s> by name is the serpent who is called 'poison of sight.'
The serpent-hood of that serpent — to that serpent, obeisance to you.
The fierce one beyond time (<s>Kālika</s>) — <s>Viṣṇu</s> with a gentle countenance.
O <s>Yamunā</s> river, remembering your <s>Kālika</s>-hymn to <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
Those who are yonder in the brightness of the sky, or those in the rays of the sun,
their seat is established in the waters — to those serpents, obeisance.
Obeisance to the serpents who are anywhere upon the earth.
Those in the atmosphere, those in heaven — to those serpents, obeisance.
Fierce-weaponed, destroyers, mighty heroes, possessing <s>māyā</s> (magical power), strong, desiring [victory],
the gods who have overcome the <s>Asuras</s> — do you, O <s>Maghavan</s> (bountiful <s>Indra</s>), ward them off with the thunderbolt. (p.87)
He whose ordinance the waters attend, in whose ordinance all cattle go,
in whose ordinance [all] is established as the abode of nourishment — that <s>Sarasvant</s> I invoke for aid.
At the sacrifice, in the heaven, in the seat of men, on the earth. //18
Speak forth, O frog (<s>maṇḍūkī</s>); proclaim the rain, O <s>tādurī</s>.
In the middle of the lake, swim, drawing in your four feet. O <s>Indra</s> and <s>Soma</s>, burn the <s>rakṣas</s> (demon), press it down. //19 (p.88)
<s>Khila</s> III, <s>Anukramaṇī</s> (Index)

Praise forth the abundantly generous <s>Indra</s>, as you know how.
He who, <s>Maghavan</s> (the bountiful), richly abundant, bestows upon the singers as if with a thousand.
As if with a hundred hosts he advances boldly, slaying the <s>Vṛtras</s> (foes) for the worshipper.
Like streams from a mountain, the gifts of the greatly nourishing one flow forth.
The pressed <s>Soma</s> drops call you, O <s>Indra</s>, to intoxication, O lover of hymns (<s>Girvaṇas</s>).
Like waters, O wielder of the thunderbolt, they fill the pond of your dwelling, O hero, for [your] bounty.
Drink the most delicious [<s>Soma</s>] of the great one, [which is] irresistible, carrying across, eager to speak.
You who, becoming intoxicated, bestow upon us — boldly, like small [streams], by yourself.
Let [<s>Indra</s>], carried by his steed, come to our praise, propelled as a horse by the pressers [of <s>Soma</s>].
When, O self-nourished one, the milch-cows delight you among the <s>Kaṇvas</s>, O <s>Indra</s> — your gifts. //1
Like a fierce hero, with reverence we approach the mighty, unfailing treasure-bearer.
Like water-vessels, O thunderbolt-wielder, your praises stream down from on high, O <s>Indra</s>.
Whether now, or at the sacrifice, or upon the earth,
from there come to our sacrifice with swift [horses], O fierce one, with towering ones.
Swift are the tawny [horses] that are your steeds, like winds driving forward,
with whom you encompass the offspring of man, with whom you survey all the heaven.
This much of your bounty, rich in cattle, we beseech, O <s>Indra</s>.
As you helped <s>Etaśa</s> in the contest for wealth, as [you helped] <s>Vaśa</s> in the cattle-pen of ten,
as among the <s>Kaṇvas</s>, O <s>Maghavan</s>, [you helped] <s>Trasadasyu</s>, as in <s>Paktha</s>'s cattle-pen of ten,
as in <s>Gośarya</s>'s [domain], for <s>Asanī</s> and <s>Ṛjiśvan</s>, O <s>Indra</s> — [grant us] wealth in cattle and gold. //
Praise forth the well-heard, abundantly generous <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>) for [our] help.
He who bestows desirable wealth upon the presser and the praiser, as if with a thousand.
His weapons are of a hundred hosts, irresistible — great are the refreshments of <s>Indra</s>.
Like <s>Śini</s>, the bountiful one swells among the generous when the pressed [<s>Soma</s> drops] have gladdened him.
When the pressed <s>Soma</s> drops have gladdened him regarding the dear one,
like water, the pressing has been set down — come to me, O dwelling one, like a milch-cow to the worshipper.
Your praises stream forth with the sweet [<s>Soma</s>], calling the irresistible one for protection.
The <s>Soma</s> drops calling you, O dwelling one, O <s>Indra</s>, have placed [you] among the hymns of praise.
Come to us, O [<s>Indra</s>] of the good sacrifice, rushing like a horse to the <s>Soma</s>.
When, O self-nourished one, those who celebrate delight you with offerings, you take pleasure in the call at the community sacrifice. //3
Praise forth the fierce hero, seeking wealth, the mighty one of great bounty.
Like a water-vessel, O thunderbolt-wielder, you have ever filled [the worshipper] from on high with wealth for the devotee.
Whether now in the distance, or on the earth, or in heaven,
yoking your tawny [horses], O <s>Indra</s>, great one, come with towering, fierce ones.
Your tawny steeds are chariot-worthy, unerring — they carry the force of the wind.
With whom you brought low the <s>Dāsyu</s> (foe) of man, with whom you survey the heaven.
This much of your newest [bounty], O <s>Vasu</s> (wealth-giver), may we know, O hero,
as you helped <s>Medhyātithi</s>, O <s>Maghavan</s>, as [you helped] <s>Nipātithi</s> in the [contest for] wealth,
as among the <s>Kaṇvas</s>, O <s>Maghavan</s>, in <s>Medha</s>'s rite — O home-dweller, in the long ceremony,
as in <s>Gośarya</s>'s [domain], the praises, O stone-armed one — [grant] to me the cow-wealth, the splendor of <s>Hari</s> (<s>Indra</s>). //4 (p.90)
As among <s>Manu</s> <s>Sāṃvaraṇa</s>, you drank the pressed <s>Soma</s>, O <s>Indra</s>,
among <s>Nipātithi</s>, O <s>Maghavan</s>, among <s>Medhyātithi</s>, among <s>Puṣṭigu</s> and <s>Śruṣṭigu</s> together.
<s>Pārṣadvāna</s> restored <s>Praskaṇva</s>, who lay helpless, reviving him.
The seer gained thousands of cattle, and also for the <s>Dasyu</s> [came] the wolf.
He who wins not by hymns alone, the discerning one, the inspirer of seers —
to that <s>Indra</s> speak forth with a new thought, who manifests [himself] for the feast.
For whom they chanted the seven-headed hymn, the threefold [hymn] in the highest place,
he indeed has made all these worlds resound — [his] manly power was born then.
He who is the giver of riches to us — that <s>Indra</s> we invoke.
For we know his newest favor — may we reach the cattle-rich pen. //5
He to whom you, O <s>Vasu</s>, bestow for giving — he attains the increase of wealth.
You, O <s>Maghavan</s>, O <s>Indra</s>, O lover of hymns, we who have <s>Soma</s> invoke.
Never are you a barren cow; you do not fail the worshipper, O <s>Indra</s>.
Again and again, O <s>Maghavan</s>, more and more — the gift of the god is asked for.
He who advanced mightily against <s>Krivi</s>, making <s>Śuṣṇa</s> resound with blows,
when indeed he propped apart the heaven, extending it — then was born the earthly one.
He whose [servants] are all this noble <s>Ārya</s> and <s>Dāsa</s>, the treasure-keeper, the enemy —
even across, O <s>Ārya</s>, in the shining <s>Ruśama</s>, in <s>Pavīravi</s> — for you that wealth is churned.
Eager, honey-dripping, ghee-streaming, the inspired ones chanted the hymn.
In us has wealth spread, the manly power of the bull; in us the pressed <s>Soma</s> drops [have streamed]. //6 (p.91)
As among <s>Manu Vivasvat</s> you drank the pressed <s>Soma</s>, O <s>Śakra</s>,
as in <s>Trita</s> you delighted, O <s>Indra</s>, as in <s>Āyu</s> you rejoice together — [so here].
Among <s>Pṛṣadhra</s>, <s>Medhya</s>, <s>Mātariśvan</s>, O <s>Indra</s>, you found delight in the pressed [<s>Soma</s>].
As [you drank] <s>Soma</s> among <s>Daśasipra</s>, <s>Daśoṇya</s>, <s>Syūmaraśmi</s>, <s>Ṛjīṇaśa</s> —
he who held the sole hymns of praise, who boldly drank the <s>Soma</s>,
for whom <s>Viṣṇu</s> strode his three steps, according to the ordinances of <s>Mitra</s> —
he in whose hymns of praise you delight, O <s>Indra</s>, in the prize-contest, O prize-winning one, O hundred-powered —
you we invoke, like a good milch-cow for the milker, in [songs of] glory.
He who is the giver of riches to us — he is our father, great, fierce, sovereign, the maker.
The irresistible, fierce <s>Maghavan</s>, richly abundant — he gives us cattle and horses. //7
He to whom you, O <s>Vasu</s>, are gracious for giving — he promotes the increase of wealth.
Desiring riches, we invoke <s>Indra</s>, the lord of wealth, the hundred-powered, with hymns.
Never do you neglect [us]; you protect both races (<s>janmanī</s>).
The fourth <s>Āditya</s> pressing is your <s>Indra</s>-power — it has taken its stand in immortality in heaven.
O <s>Maghavan</s>, O <s>Indra</s>, O lover of hymns, you who bestow upon the generous worshipper —
hear our songs and well-fashioned praise, O <s>Vasu</s>, like [those of] <s>Kaṇva</s>, hear [our] call.
The ancient hymn of praise has been proclaimed; speak the sacred word (<s>brahman</s>) to <s>Indra</s>.
The many and great [praises] of <s>Ṛta</s> (cosmic order) have been sung; the wisdom of the singer has been let loose.
<s>Indra</s> has shaken forth the great treasures, and the two worlds, and the sun.
The bright, shining, cow-voiced <s>Soma</s> drops have gladdened <s>Indra</s>. //8 (p.92)
The highest among the bountiful, the greatest among the bulls,
the greatest breaker of strongholds, O <s>Maghavan</s>, O <s>Indra</s>, finder of cattle — we beg the lord of wealth.
He who came to [help] <s>Kutsa</s>, <s>Atithigva</s>, <s>Ardhayu</s>, growing day by day —
you, the tawny-horsed, the hundred-powered, desiring prizes, we invoke.
The stones pour upon us the essence of sweet [<s>Soma</s>].
Those who press [<s>Soma</s>] in the distance among peoples, and those who are near — the <s>Soma</s> drops,
smite all enmities and ward them off; may all press forth the good [<s>Soma</s>].
Even in the most excellent [offerings], your intoxicating portions — where you satiate yourself with <s>Soma</s>.
O <s>Indra</s>, come nearer, with measured wisdoms and aids,
with the most auspicious of auspicious assistances, with the most sleep-giving of sleep-givers.
Make the swift racer, the lord of men, the beholder of all people, partaking [of <s>Soma</s>] among the clans.
Go forth by your powers, [O <s>Indra</s>]; those who praise you in hymns purify your purpose in succession.
May we be your best [allies] for protection; may we be [foremost] in your contests,
with fire-oblations and divine invocations — the victorious ones have been heard.
For I, O possessor of tawny steeds, am the prayer-winner who races to the contest with constant aids.
You alone, even that one — I, desiring horses, desiring cattle, place at the forefront of [my] thoughts. //10
This your heroic deed, O <s>Indra</s>, the poets celebrate with songs.
They, chanting, have obtained nourishing strength, dripping with ghee; they have approached with praises.
They approach <s>Indra</s> for protection with good deeds — in whose pressed [<s>Soma</s>] you delight.
As among <s>Saṃvarta</s> you found no delight, as among <s>Kṛśa</s> — even so in us, O <s>Indra</s>, find delight.
May all the gods, united, come to us, come near to us.
May the <s>Vasus</s>, the <s>Rudras</s> come for our aid; may the <s>Maruts</s> hear [our] call.
<s>Pūṣan</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Sarasvatī</s> — may they favor my invocation; may the Seven Rivers [favor it].
The Waters, the Wind, the Mountains, the Lord of the Forest — may the Earth hear [our] call. //11
That bounty of yours which exists, O <s>Indra</s>, most bountiful among the generous —
by that be awake to us for increase, as a companion in fellowship — a portion for giving, O slayer of <s>Vṛtra</s>.
O lord of the contest, lord of men, you alone have bestowed upon us prizes, O wise-minded one.
We, through oblations and divine invocations, having won [the prize], worship.
For there are, O noble one, blessings of <s>Indra</s> for the lifespan of people.
Come to us, O <s>Maghavan</s>, for [our] protection; yield the overflowing refreshment.
We would worship you, O <s>Indra</s>, with praises; you [be] ours, O <s>Śatakratu</s> (hundred-powered one).
Bestow upon <s>Praskaṇva</s> a great, mighty, irresistible, generous gift. ||12
Abundant indeed is the heroic power of <s>Indra</s>—it manifestly conquers.
Your bounty [was given], O <s>Dasyave Vṛka</s>.
A hundred white bulls shine in heaven like stars.
With greatness they have indeed stood firm.
A hundred bamboo [staves], a hundred dogs, a hundred hides were given.
A hundred tufts of <s>balbaja</s> grass [were given] to me, and four hundred red [cows].
You are possessed of good gods, O descendants of <s>Kaṇva</s>, moving from stage to stage of life.
Eager like horses.
Then indeed they celebrated from the seventh [offering], and undiminished, great renown.
The dark ones traversed the paths—one cannot even reach [them] with the eye. ||13
Your generous, irresistible bounty was seen, O <s>Dasyave Vṛka</s>.
Strength like heaven in breadth.
<s>Pūtakratu Dasyave Vṛka</s> [gave] ten thousands to me.
From perpetual wealth they were generous.
A hundred donkeys [were given] to me, a hundred woolly [sheep].
A hundred garlands upon gifts.
There too breathed forth the gift of <s>Pūtakratu</s>, clearly manifest.
Like a herd of horses.
<s>Agni</s>, the discerning one, the bearer of oblations, was recognized—he with the fair chariot, <s>Sumadrathaḥ</s>.
<s>Agni</s> shone brightly with [his] brilliant radiance—great like <s>Sūrya</s> in heaven, <s>Sūrya</s> shone.
O <s>Agni</s>, come with the [other] fires. ||14
You stood by the drop (<s>Drapsa</s>) fighting with a bow, O <s>Maghavan</s>, [coming] from [the river] <s>Aṃśumatī</s>.
O hero, the waters [flow] forth; the winner of treasures—O <s>Indra</s>, those are your manifold mighty deeds, O <s>Purukṛt</s>.
You indeed, being born for the seven [rivers]. ||15
The <s>Pāvamānī</s> [verses] are conducive to well-being, yielding abundantly, for they drip with ghee.
The essence gathered by the sages—the immortal nectar placed among the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>.
May the <s>Pāvamānī</s> [verses] grant us this world and the other.
May the goddesses, gathered with the gods, fulfill our desires.
By which purifier the gods always purify themselves,
may the <s>Pāvamānī</s> [verses], by that thousand-streamed [purifier], purify me.
The purifier belonging to <s>Prajāpati</s>, with a hundred stretches, golden—
by that, we who know <s>Brahman</s> purify the pure <s>Brahman</s>.
May <s>Indra</s> purify me with good guidance, <s>Soma</s> with well-being, <s>Varuṇa</s> with rectitude.
May King <s>Yama</s> purify me with life-refreshing [waters]; may <s>Jātavedas</s> purify me with invigorating [power].
The <s>Pāvamānī</s> [verses], conducive to well-being, by which one goes to <s>Nandana</s> (paradise),
and enjoys sacred offerings, and attains immortality.
[Let] the honey-rich [offerings proceed] forth toward the god. ||16
Whatever fierce sin [was contracted] while I dwelt in the womb, and whatever other while being born,
and whatever of mine while born and while growing—that I purify with the <s>Pāvamānī</s> [verses].
Whatever word of mine was not fulfilled for mother and father, whatever [harm I caused to] stationary and moving [beings],
whatever hurtful speech of mine toward anyone—that I purify with the <s>Pāvamānī</s> [verses].
From buying and selling, from defects of birth, from [improper] eating and being fed, from accepting [improper] gifts,
and also from not feeding [the deserving] and from cruelty—that I purify with the <s>Pāvamānī</s> [verses].
From cow-slaying, from thievery, from the killing of a woman, and whatever sin [arising therefrom],
and evil done by [one's] conduct—that I purify with the <s>Pāvamānī</s> [verses].
From slaying a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, from drinking liquor, from stealing gold, from intercourse with an outcaste woman,
and from approaching the teacher's wife—that I purify with the <s>Pāvamānī</s> [verses].
From child-killing, from slaying mother or father, from stealing land, from intercourse and sexual union with [persons of] all classes,
and from accepting [gifts] from sinners—instantly they drive away all evil deeds; that I purify with the <s>Pāvamānī</s> [verses].
Whatever food is offered without [proper] <s>mantras</s> into the fire (<s>Hutāśana</s>),
and sin accumulated over a year—that I purify with the <s>Pāvamānī</s> [verses].
Whatever was badly sacrificed, badly studied, and sin committed through ignorance,
and those unworthy ones who should not be caused to sacrifice—that I purify with the <s>Pāvamānī</s> [verses].
The sources of <s>Ṛta</s> (cosmic order), the abode of immortality, of sacred fragrance for all the gods—
may those waters carry away [our] sin; with faith I go to the world of the virtuous; that I purify with the <s>Pāvamānī</s> [verses].
[Editorial note: = verse 5 of the manuscript]
