Whoever meditates on the <s>Pāvamānī</s> [verses], the ancestors, the gods, and <s>Sarasvatī</s>—
milk, ghee, honey, and water would attend upon [his] ancestors.
The sages performed <s>tapas</s> (austerity), all desiring to conquer heaven.
But supreme among austerities is to recite the <s>Pāvamānī</s> <s>ṛcs</s> (verses).
Those wise ones who recite the <s>Pāvamānī</s> [hymn], the supreme <s>Brahman</s>—
for seven births one becomes a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, rich in wealth, having mastered the <s>Vedas</s>.
These are six hundred <s>Pāvamānī</s> verses, increasing by tens.
Offering these [into the fire] and reciting [them], one conquers the terrible fear of death.
The <s>Pāvamānī</s> [hymn], the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, the bright, eternal light—
milk, ghee, honey, and water would attend upon the sages of that [reciter].
Like <s>Iḍā</s> indeed—may she follow you two with ghee; at whose footstep the godly ones purify [themselves].
With ghee-footsteps, of the <s>Śakvarī</s> [metre], with <s>Soma</s> on her back, the all-divine one stood near the sacrifice.
The all-divine purifying goddess came, in whom these many bodies [are] with outspread backs.
Rejoicing with her in the middle [pressings], may we be lords of wealth.
Run forth, settle around the vessel. ||17
Where the world-dwellers who have abandoned the body, conquered by faith and <s>tapas</s> (austerity), [reside],
and where radiance and <s>Brahman</s> [dwell]—there make me immortal; flow around for <s>Indra</s>, O <s>Indu</s> (Soma).
Where the great-souled gods [dwell], with <s>Indra</s>, together with the hosts of <s>Maruts</s>,
and where <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s> [dwell]—there make me immortal; flow around for <s>Indra</s>, O <s>Indu</s>.
Where that supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s> is glorified in the world,
by the gods through meritorious deeds—there make me immortal; flow around for <s>Indra</s>, O <s>Indu</s>. Where there are joys and delights— ||18
The active [waters], flowing by day and by night,
I, of excellent purpose, invoke the divine [waters] for protection.
May I indeed turn a friend to friendship. ||19
Come, O <s>Indra</s>, with [your] wealth-bearing chariot; drink the <s>Soma</s> together for exhilaration.
Having drunk [it] into [your] hearts, delighting with the <s>Maruts</s>, go forth for the slaying of <s>Vṛtra</s>, O wielder of the <s>vajra</s>.
O <s>Indra</s>, drink this <s>Soma</s>. ||20
I place your heart under my vow; may your mind follow my mind.
Take delight in my speech with single-minded devotion; may <s>Bṛhaspati</s> yoke you to me.
<s>Dhātṛ</s> gave you to me; may <s>Dhātṛ</s> place you [under] me.
<s>Pradhātṛ</s> gave you forth to me; <s>Anumati</s> gave you to me.
Be well-disposed with good will; be well-disposed with [your] own consent.
Make this [person] favorable to me—through speech, through sight, through mind, restrained toward me.
I have brought your heart; may that become my heart.
And may my heart be your heart.
Heart by heart, breath by breath, I have seized [you].
I seize [your] sight with [my] sight; I seize [your] mind with [my] mind.
Intention, thought, sight, hearing, and also strength—
with that splendor which the gods attained, I bind your mind.
With a jewel made of food, with a thread of <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath), variegated,
I bind your heart and mind with a knot of truth.
[There is] turning toward, turning back; by me [there is] your winning over.
<s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>, the two <s>Aśvins</s>, <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, and <s>Dhātṛ</s> have made [this charm].
Whatever thought by which you speak, by which another bewitches you—
bring all that here, O <s>Agni</s>; you are to be satisfied by [this] devotee.
Following the forest, good forest, upward forest, forest—
behold the forms of the hot [offering]; with that I bind your mind. ||22
May cattle come together to me; may herbs come together to me.
May kings come together to me, as I desire.
May I be of endless growth for you; may my heart be without limit.
May the assembly and the council—both daughters of <s>Prajāpati</s>, of one mind—protect [me].
At gatherings, at each step—[let there be] beauty; homage to <s>Vaiśvānara</s> (universal fire).
...by [that] step, I have gathered your vital breaths.
And also I gather this which is among other people.
I [have become] your sight with [my] sight; I [have become] your mind with [my] mind.
I, in the form of a <s>Gandharva</s>, continually turn [your heart] toward me. ||23
Destroyed is [your] thought [elsewhere], destroyed is [your] mind [elsewhere]; destroyed is your mind toward others.
Among all the black-haired ones, destroyed is your mind toward others.
Look only at me and at the sun—never at a third.
You are remembrance, the generator of desire; may your desire be in me.
Whatever desirable mind of yours has been placed in many worlds—
like rivers [flowing] to the ocean, we make all of that follow [back to me].
I set your heart ablaze; with my fire we kindle [it].
This is the ember of your heart; I am aflame—you are burning.
Of you, burning because of me—may the fire not be satisfied with the offering; may the earth be satisfied with the offering. ||24
May <s>Dhātṛ</s> direct your thought and your mind toward me.
May your thought be dependent on me; may your mind reach [its end] in me.
Turned toward me [are] your vital breaths... [text incomplete]
[Lacuna in manuscript]
Lost is your longing for another; may your mind delight in me.
...mind... [text incomplete]
Your sight, hearing, and learning—all of yours I take.
The sage born from the heart... [text incomplete]
That very [sage], the seer of meaning, they placed in these hearts.
The all-knowing, all-seeing [one]—may he accomplish our rites.
Those... entered, O <s>Jātavedas</s>—<s>Agni</s>, the deed of the ill-hearted one— [text partially lost]
I offer the allotted portion of those; may the gods satisfy me with all desires.
Gathered through the <s>tapas</s> (austerity) of the <s>Bhṛgus</s> and <s>Aṅgirasas</s>,
and of those who favor the <s>Kuśikas</s>—I turn your mind [toward me].
Whatever desirable mind of yours has been placed in many worlds—
that we turn back to you—[we,] the irresistible, the daylight-born <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.
Whatever charm of persuasion <s>Kakṣīvān</s>, the son of the <s>Aṅgirasas</s>, knew—
with that, may the <s>Viśvedevas</s> (All-Gods) today make [her] beloved to us, may they win [her] over. ||26
Goad this one, O <s>Gṛhapati</s> (lord of the house), from [her] bed among kinsmen.
Seizing [her] by the neck, arise; by the feet, do not let [her] rest.
May the <s>Maruts</s> dig up [and bring] forth, forth from the ocean, the curd.
May this <s>Agni</s> burn with resolve; may <s>Sūrya</s> scorch with resolve.
As you dry up a woman heated for the sake of a love-bed—
thus dry up our enemies; serve [us] by day and by night.
O <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>, make this [woman] for me; let [her heart] be cast away [from others] by thought.
Having given, having drunk, having placed at the front—so that by divine power [she is] in [my] control.
Make the others servants, O divine one; [make] the dependents subject to [my] will.
Standing with [your] foot upon [their] head, together with [their] lineage, for perpetual years. ||27
By the seasons and the seasonal [offerings], together with lifespan and splendor,
by the brilliance of the year—by that, purify me together [with them].
By this sacred prayer, O <s>Agni</s>, you and this <s>Indra</s> [are] praised by us.
Grant him supreme sovereignty and lordship among his own [people].
O <s>Agni</s>, strike down the gathered arrows at every vital spot.
Drive the <s>khadira</s>-wood stake into the heart of our enemy; do not let [him] rest.
The earth is supported by truth. ||28
Be firm, O prosperous one, in me; <s>Bṛhaspati</s> has given you to me.
With me as your husband, rich in progeny, live together a hundred autumns.
For indeed they have been released from the presser. ||29
Be unwidowed for a hundred years and more, O faithful one.
Splendid and glorious, a wife devoted to <s>Dharma</s>, devoted to your husband.
May you bear many sons and never obtain sorrow anywhere.
May your husband always be a <s>Soma</s>-drinker, devoted to <s>Dharma</s>.
Be the mother of eight sons, and be fortunate and devoted to your husband.
Always delighting the hearts of your husband, father, and brother.
As <s>Indrāṇī</s> is to <s>Indra</s>, as <s>Śrī</s> is to <s>Śrīdhara</s>,
as <s>Gaurī</s> is to <s>Śaṅkara</s>—so may you be to your husband.
As <s>Anasūyā</s> was to <s>Atri</s>, and <s>Arundhatī</s> to <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>,
as <s>Satī</s> was to <s>Kauśika</s> (Viśvāmitra)—so may you be to your husband.
One alone is <s>Agni</s>, kindled in many forms; one is <s>Sūrya</s>, pervading all.
One alone is <s>Uṣas</s> (Dawn), illuminating all this; one alone has become all this.
Whom the priests, fashioning in many ways, with one mind, carry forward in this sacrifice,
the learned <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> who sits engaged—what then is the knowledge of the sacrificer?
As much as the countenance of Dawn. ||30
We have flown up from the dwelling-place like birds; may the <s>Bhṛgus</s>, thinking [thus], release [us].
O <s>Purūravas</s>, go back home again; [this] mind of a mortal should go to the gods' heaven. I shall proclaim to you the great two tawny steeds at the great assembly. ||31
Whatever [wrong] we have done, whatever sin we have committed,
may the herbs protect us from that misfortune and sin.
O <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, approach the gods for me. ||32
That army of the enemies, O <s>Maruts</s>, comes against us, contending with its might.
Hide it with darkness, with the hostile covering, so that none of them may know the other.
May the enemies be blind, headless like serpents.
Of those burnt by you, O <s>Agni</s>, may <s>Indra</s> slay the best of the best. ||33
<s>Brahman</s> (the sacred word) was born first in the east, from the boundary, the radiant <s>Vena</s> revealed it.
Its deepest foundations are the highest forms; from the existent and from the non-existent [it reveals] the womb.
This sovereignty goes to the father first, to the firstborn; the earthly dwellings have stood firm.
For him, this radiant invocation and the hot [milk offering]—they mingle for the first one to bestow.
The great one established the great heaven; the father, born wide, [established] the earthly seat and the atmosphere.
From the depth he rose powerfully by birth; <s>Bṛhaspati</s> is the deity, the sovereign of that.
I praise that god <s>Savitar</s>, of the two lights, of wise purpose—
I praise the true-natured, treasure-holding one, the beloved wise thought.
Whose upward, immortal radiance has shone forth, in his own realm—
the golden-handed one measured out, of good purpose, the luminous heaven. ||34
Those two, <s>Sūrya</s> (Sun) and <s>Candramas</s> (Moon), knowing the paths, [shine with] a great, rich, brilliant light in heaven.
Moving with the same self, companions in movement—whose vow no one ever subdues, of the two gods.
You both traverse the two ends—like the reins of heaven extending across the ocean.
Both becoming the two worlds, of wise purpose—<s>Sūrya</s> and <s>Candramas</s> move with imperishable mind.
Brilliant lords, knowing all, both of heaven—<s>Sūrya</s>, both, and <s>Candramas</s>, far-seeing.
Both all-beautiful, spacious, both choiceworthy—may they protect us, the mindful ones, of great vow.
All-pervading, crossing over, the two transcendent ones—knowers of the sun, many-rayed, for seeing.
For <s>Sūrya</s> and <s>Candramas</s>, rich in goods, brilliant to behold, wise—both move together through heaven. ||35
His fame the seven rivers bear; Heaven and Earth [reveal] his visible form.
May <s>Sūrya</s> and <s>Candramas</s> look upon us with faith—O <s>Indra</s>, the two move beyond confusion.
The earlier and the later move by their <s>Māyā</s> (wondrous power)—like two children playing, they go around the sacrifice.
One beholds all the worlds; the other, ordering the seasons, is born again.
The <s>Soma</s> has been pressed, O much-invoked one, for you. ||36
IV. <s>Adhyāya</s> (Chapter). (Anukramaṇī).
Oṃ. [The hymn beginning with] 'ā yasmin'—one [verse] in <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>. 'tad ā rātri'—a group of four, the first in <s>Bṛhatī</s>. 'arvāñcam'—one in <s>Triṣṭubh</s>.
In whom, at the gods' feast, may the sons come together, united.
Unconquerable through praise, heard, [he] dares boldly.
I move with the <s>Rudras</s>, with the <s>Vasus</s>. ||1
O <s>Rātri</s> (Night), [you fill] the earthly realm; the father's abodes have been filled.
The great one occupies the seats of heaven; the fierce darkness turns about.
Those who are your watchers, O Night, the ninety and nine yoked ones—
may there be eighty, and also eight, and seventy-seven.
I take refuge in Night, the mother, the resting-place of all beings,
the auspicious, fortunate, dark one—the night of the entire world.
She who puts to rest, who restrains, garlanded with planets and stars—
I have taken refuge in the auspicious Night; O blessed one, may we reach the far shore.
O <s>Agni</s>, may my splendor prevail in invocations. ||2
With devotion I shall praise the goddess, the protectress, dear to the <s>Bahvṛcas</s> (Ṛgvedins),
<s>Durgā</s>, equal to a thousand—we press <s>Soma</s> for <s>Jātavedas</s> (Agni).
For the peace of the twice-born, the sages have taken refuge [in her].
You were born from the <s>Ṛgveda</s>; the <s>Veda</s> burns up the hostile ones.
Those <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> who take refuge in you, O goddess, the carrier of oblations—
whether of little learning or much learning—may she carry us across all difficulties.
Those twice-born who praise her—fire-colored, beautiful, gentle—
<s>Agni</s> carries [them] across difficulties, like a boat across the river, beyond all misfortune.
In hardships, in rough terrain, in terrible battle, in the enemy's siege,
in the fall of fire and thieves, in warding off evil planets—for warding off evil planets, Oṃ, salutation.
In hardships, in rough places, in battles, and in forests,
having bewildered [the enemies] they take refuge—create fearlessness for me, create fearlessness for me, Oṃ, salutation.
The hairy one, [named] 'Fifth' among all beings—by that name also—
may that goddess protect me from all directions on all sides, protect on all sides, Oṃ, salutation.
Her who is fire-colored, blazing with <s>tapas</s> (austerity), daughter of <s>Virocana</s>, delighted in the fruits of action—
I take refuge in the goddess <s>Durgā</s>; salutation to you who ferry across, salutation to you who ferry across.
<s>Durgā</s> in difficult places—may the goddess be for our protection.
Whoever recites this holy <s>Durgā Stava</s> (praise of Durgā) every night,
<s>Rātri</s> [is the seer], <s>Kuśika</s> or <s>Saubhara</s>; or it is <s>Bhāradvājī Rātri</s>; the <s>Rātri Stava</s> is in <s>Gāyatrī</s> [metre].
One should recite the <s>Rātri Sūkta</s> always; the proper time arrives [for it].
We call <s>Indra</s> hither from there, he who wins cows, wins wealth, wins horses.
Enjoy this our sacrifice at the invocation; here we make you, O possessor of tawny steeds, the altar-knower. ||3
Salutation to you, O lightning; salutation to you, O thunder.
Salutation to you, O thunderstone, who hurls me with evil fate.
Salutation to you, O son of the cloud, from whom you gather <s>tapas</s> (heat).
Be gracious to our bodies; [grant] fearlessness to our cattle.
O son of the cloud, salutation indeed to you; we make salutation to your weapon and to your heat.
We know your supreme name, hidden in secret; you are hidden within the ocean.
She whom the gods brought forth—[O goddess,] accept the thought [of one] composing prayer for the winning of the prize.
She, gracious to us at the assembly, being praised—salutation be to you, O goddess. ||4
The enemies fashion for us a cruel <s>Kṛtyā</s> (sorcery), like a bride.
By the sacred word (<s>Brahman</s>) we drive her back; may she reach her creator in return.
Having a head, having ears, of all forms, fear-inspiring—
I send you forth today—go, yoke yourself with the inauspicious ones.
With whatever mind you speak contrarily, O malevolent one,
that very [intention], O <s>Kṛtyā</s>, [return] here to him—do not [harm] us, the sinless ones.
Turn back upon the maker; cast out by us with force.
Take away his lifespan, and his offspring, O devourer of men.
O <s>Kṛtyā</s>, he who made you here—go to him, repeatedly.
Destroy the enemies, the sorceries, and all the sorceresses. ||5
Quickly turn back, O <s>Kṛtyā</s>, to the very house of the maker.
Drive away his cattle and destroy, and cut down his heroes.
Whoever sends you forth, O <s>Kṛtyā</s>—
He who joined your limbs together, like <s>Ṛbhu</s> with thought [joining] a chariot—
go to him; there is your person; unknown to you is that person. ||6
...or whoever injures [us]—
you, like a fire kindled from a tree, inquire of his body, being angered.
...to that evildoer of yours—
you too, O <s>Kṛtyā</s>, [bearing] flames—not the least bit of his head [shall remain].
Those auspicious paths of ours that go far to the distance—
by those, O divine one, send away the hostile sorceries; turn [them] back.
Whoever among us, any enemy or foe, even in thought assails [us]—
whether standing far or near—drink the blood of his heart.
By whom you have been sent forth, O <s>Kṛtyā</s>, with evil intent to destroy us—
may the autumn thunderbolt destroy both his offspring and his prosperity. ||7
Whether you come as a biped against us or as a quadruped—
cast out by us, O lawless one, [go as] an octopod to the maker's house.
He who curses us without being cursed, and he who curses us when we curse—
may he wither from the root, like a tree struck by lightning.
He whom we hate and who hates us, the malevolent one, and he who curses us—
like a crushing [pestle] for a dog, I hurl him over to death.
Whatever curse of a rival, and whatever curse of a kinsman,
and whatever an angered <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> may curse—make all that the underside.
Whether kinsman or non-kinsman, whoever assails us—
you, standing upon him, split his head with your foot, trampling. ||8
Go forth, O thousand-eyed one, having yoked the swift chariot of the curse.
O <s>Kṛtyā</s>, seeking enemies—like a she-wolf, [going to] uncovered houses.
Surround our curses [and turn them back], burning like <s>Agni</s> burns an enclosure.
Pierce the enemies alone, like the divine thunderbolt [splits] a tree.
May those who curse us, our enemies, and the sorceries—and [may] dear friends [be protected] in [our] hearts.
The crooked, smooth, and ill-intentioned—[cast them at] the kindled <s>Jātavedas</s> (fire).
Make the east free from enemies for us; make the south auspicious.
Constant safety to the west; prosperity to the north of the house.
Depart, O <s>kṛtya</s> (sorcery), do not stay! Lead [your course] like the footstep of an old man.
You are the hunter of a deer; you deserve to cut that down. || 9 ||
O inviolable-mouthed one, of terrible form, of excellent form, O destructress!
Seize back those who have been seized; take up the wondrous [weapon] yourself.
You are <s>Indra</s>, <s>Yama</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>; you are the waters, <s>Agni</s>, and also the wind.
<s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Rudra</s> and <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> and <s>Prajāpati</s>.
Turn around, turn back, O seasons, O full years.
Days and nights and years—you are the directions and intermediate directions for me.
You are <s>Indra</s>, <s>Yama</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>; you are the waters, <s>Agni</s>, and also the wind.
Having snatched away the cattle, the gods—drive away the wondrous [evil]. || 10 ||
Anointed and well-adorned, destroy all evil for us.
Know the makers of <s>kṛtyā</s>s (sorceries), those men of sinful mind.
As [an arrow] strikes one sitting in front, so that same arrow [strikes] people again and again.
Thus with you as companion, we cut down that [sorcerer]—[both] the stationary and the moving.
Rise up and depart hence! O inviolable-mouthed one, what do you desire here?
O <s>kṛtya</s>, I shall break your necks and your feet too—run away!
Our weapons are of iron; we know your joints too.
We cut down those [joints], O fierce one—if you would let us live.
Let not [the sorcery] leave over any biped; release no quadruped.
Nor kinsmen, nor followers, nor the neighborhood, nor the neighbors. || 11 ||
This [<s>kṛtya</s>] sent by one who is hostile—against whomever, in whatever manner—
from that, may he who dwells within me drive you back accordingly.
Thus you are crushed by us in every way, O goddess, by the <s>Brahman</s> (sacred word).
Having made [the sorcery] resort to that [sender], strike down the sinner for us.
May all the gods destroy him; <s>Brahman</s> is my inner armor.
Just as a tree struck by lightning dries up from the root,
so may he dry up who intends evil for me.
Just as [the sorcery], having been sent back, runs back toward that very [sender],
may the evil run to that very one who intends evil for me.
May <s>Kuvīra</s> and comfort, <s>Rudra</s> and rejoicing destroy [the evil].
<s>Brahman</s> is my inner armor; peace is my inner armor; heat is my inner armor. || 12 ||
[Grant] longevity, splendor, abundance of wealth, and growth.
May this gold, splendid, enter me for victory.
The loud steed, conqueror in battle, victorious in the assembly, wealth-winning.
All prosperities, complete, are gathered in this gold.
I have grasped this gold auspiciously, as if grasping a father's name.
By that may I make myself sun-skinned, dear to people.
Sovereignty and splendor, and the conquest that is firm for me,
the <s>Lakṣmī</s> (fortune) that is in the mouth of the kingdom—with that, O <s>Indra</s>, unite me.
The gold that was born from <s>Agni</s>—immortal [substance] born among mortals—
he who knows it is worthy of it; old age and death come to him who wears it. || 13 ||
What king <s>Varuṇa</s> knows, what the goddess <s>Sarasvatī</s> [knows],
what <s>Indra</s> the slayer of <s>Vṛtra</s> knows—may that be for my splendor and long life.
Neither <s>rakṣas</s>es (demons) nor <s>piśāca</s>s (ghouls) can overcome it, for this is the first-born power of the gods.
He who wears the gold of <s>Dakṣāyaṇā</s> makes long life among the gods, makes long life among men.
When the <s>Dākṣāyaṇā</s>s, with joyful minds, bound the gold upon him of a hundred faces—
I bind that upon myself for a hundred autumns, so that, long-lived, I may reach old age.
Drawn from ghee, sweet, golden, wealth-winning, supporting, sustaining,
rendering enemies low, destroying debts—mount upon me for great good fortune.
Make me dear among the gods; make me dear among kings.
Make me dear among all protectors; place in me radiance upon radiance.
There was neither non-being nor being. || 14 ||
The earth is [your] mother, the sky your father; <s>Aryaman</s> is your grandfather.
<s>Ghṛtācī</s> is your name; you are the sister of the gods.
He who drinks you lives; you protect the person.
You are the eternal protectress, the eternal uniter.
Whatever was done by a staff, by an arrow, or by the burning of <s>Vāru</s>—
you are the remedy for that, O herbs, the remedy upon the ridge.
You fly from tree to tree, like a maiden going to the trees.
Victorious, standing firm—<s>Saṃjayā</s> (conqueress) is your name.
From the auspicious <s>plakṣa</s> (fig) tree descend, from the <s>aśvattha</s>, <s>khadira</s>, <s>dhava</s>,
from the auspicious <s>parṇa</s> and <s>nyagrodha</s> (banyan)—may <s>Arundhatī</s> heal me.
You fly to the blood of the horse; you alight upon that leaf.
Flowing, falling, reddish—may <s>Arundhatī</s> heal me.
O golden-leaved one, O fortunate one, O smooth one, O hairy-chested one,
you are the sister of the waters, O <s>lākṣā</s> (lac); the wind became your breath.
In your friendship, O <s>Indra</s>, [these are] the bearers. || 15 ||
Night is [your] mother, the sky your father; <s>Aryaman</s> is your grandfather.
<s>Śilādī</s> is your name; you are the sister of the gods.
He who drinks you lives; you protect the person.
You are the eternal sustainer, the eternal subduer.
Whatever was done by a thorn, by burning, or by harm with violence—
you are the healer for that; <s>Niṣkṛti</s> (remedy) is your name.
You stand auspiciously by the <s>plakṣa</s> tree, the <s>aśvattha</s>, <s>khadira</s>, <s>dhava</s>,
auspiciously by the <s>nyagrodha</s> and <s>parṇa</s>—do not depart, O <s>Arundhatī</s>.
You climb from tree to tree, like a maiden seeking a husband.
Victorious, standing firm—<s>Saṃjayā</s> (conqueress) is your name.
O golden-hued one, O youthful one, of fiery energy, with hair as eyes,
you are the sister of the waters, O <s>lākṣā</s>; the wind became [your breath].
O golden-armed one, O fortunate one, O sun-hued one, most beautiful in form,
you go to truth; heal [him]; heal this human being.
<s>Ghṛtācī</s> is your name, born of a maiden; be not a dark father.
The horse of <s>Yama</s>—the fame—they sprinkled with his bone.
Having fallen from the bone of the horse, it dried upon the leaf.
Always falling, do not depart, O <s>Arundhatī</s>.
O <s>Ghṛtācī</s>, O delighter in good, O lightning-leaved <s>Arundhatī</s>,
you who are swift as a horse, you are the one who removes [disease].
What the <s>piśāca</s>s have seized while you were awake—let that come back again.
O <s>lākṣā</s>, healing all [diseases], may [she] protect along with the gods.
The <s>Aṅgiras</s>es gave me <s>medhā</s> (wisdom); the seven seers gave me <s>medhā</s>.
<s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s> [gave me] <s>medhā</s>; may <s>Dhātṛ</s> bestow <s>medhā</s> upon me.
May king <s>Varuṇa</s> [give me] <s>medhā</s>; may the goddess <s>Sarasvatī</s> [give me <s>medhā</s>].
May the two <s>Aśvin</s> gods, wearing lotus garlands, place <s>medhā</s> in me.
The <s>medhā</s> that is in the <s>Apsaras</s>es and in the <s>Gandharva</s>s, that [power of] mind,
the divine and human <s>medhā</s>—may that enter me here.
May that which <s>Manu</s> spoke be delightful; may I be able to repeat [it].
I observe what is observed; what is heard is in me. May I be united with <s>Brahman</s> through the shared vow.
My body is perceptive; my speech yields honey.
I have grown; that sun, through <s>Brahman</s>—[the faculties] are established. May what I have heard not desert me. || 16 ||
The goddess <s>Medhā</s>, trembling in the mind, delighted by the <s>Gandharva</s>s—delight in us.
Speak <s>medhā</s> for me, speak <s>śrī</s> (prosperity) for me; may I become wise, swift in movement.
The wondrous lord of the assembly, dear [to all], desired by <s>Indra</s>,
I have sought the gift of <s>medhā</s>.
May I be wise, of good mind, of beautiful appearance, faithful in thought, true in mind, of good conduct,
of great fame, retentive, eloquent—may I be master of its application.
The <s>medhā</s> that the hosts of gods and the ancestors worship—
with that <s>medhā</s>, O <s>Agni</s>, make me wise today. || 17 ||

Let the sun come from afar. <s>Agni</s>, the lord of the house, of beautiful appearance, brilliant; <s>Agni</s>, the light, is to be perceived; bear [him] upon the earth. Upon whose arrival the swift steed shakes off all hostilities on the road. Having stepped forth, O steed, upon the earth, seek <s>Agni</s> with splendor. The well-praised [fire] conquers the army, the shining one, the brilliant.

<s>Agni</s>, firmly our messenger between the two worlds, the oblation-bearer, brought the gods to the sacrifice. The inspired messenger, the adorned, the worshipful, the wise poet—like <s>Apnavāna</s>, like <s>Aurva</s>, like <s>Bhṛgu</s>, like <s>Jamadagni</s>—

Your <s>Agni</s> is the great queen, the smoke-bannered, awakening at dawn; <s>Vaiśvānara</s> (universal fire) has looked upon the front of the dawns, has stridden forth, the wealth-giver, the swift steed. In the good world of the meritorious on earth—from there let us dig up the beautiful-faced <s>Agni Vaiśvānara</s>, climbing to one's own [heaven], upon the vault of heaven. Prosper here with prosperity; restore to us what was lost; restore to us wealth.

Indeed the gods—the fat, the self-controlled one—the roaring one did not impel the regions. O <s>Agni</s>, consider; you, O <s>Agni</s>, the keeper of vows, the pure one. O <s>Agni</s>, bring the gods here, and our sacrifice and oblation. Bearing the vows, the protector of vows, uninjured, sacrifice to the gods for us, the ageless one, rich in heroes. Bestowing treasures, gracious <s>Agni</s>, protect us for life, O <s>Jātavedas</s>.

The divine <s>Agni Sviṣṭakṛt</s> (maker of good offerings), of good wealth, joyous, poet, of true thought, the officiant, the <s>Hotṛ</s> priest's <s>Hotṛ</s>—the offerings that O <s>Agni</s> you performed for the gods, those you satisfied, those who delighted in your priesthood—may the gods-going <s>hotra</s>s in heaven—among the gods, send forth the sacrifice. And <s>Agni Sviṣṭakṛt</s> became the <s>Hotṛ</s> priest, in the winning of treasures, in the bestowing of wealth—speak the word of homage.

May [the fire] carry away all evil. We invoke <s>Agni</s> with songs. <s>Agni</s> with bright flame—the great sun shone, the sun shone in heaven. Fed with oblations of ghee—the luminous sun does not [cease] shining. Place oblations in <s>Agni</s>; place sacred utterances in <s>Agni</s> alone. The great [<s>Agni</s>] at the sacrifice—the ghee of the generous worshiper—thus you, O <s>Agni</s>, the calf has strengthened with his powers and songs. Proclaim thus the great things. || 18 ||
<s>Vena</s> (the longing one) perceived that—the knower of the world—where the universe has one nest.
This cow milked [the offerings] as she was being born; the flocks praised [her], the finder of the sun.
The <s>Gandharva</s>, knowing the immortal, proclaimed that which is hidden in the secret place.
Three steps of his are hidden in the secret [place]; he who knows them becomes the father's father.
He is the kinsman of being, the progenitor, the ordainer; he knows all the abodes, all the worlds.
Where the gods, having attained immortality, soared up to the third abode.
From your eyes, from your nostrils— || 19 ||
<s>Vena</s> perceives that supreme abode where the universe has one nest.
This cow milked [the offerings] as she was being born; the knower of the sun—<s>Virāj</s> praised.
Having known the immortal separately, the <s>Gandharva</s> [declared] the supreme abode, that which is hidden in the secret [place].
Three steps are struck in the secret places; he who knows them becomes the father's father.
He is our kinsman, the progenitor, the arranger; he knows all the abodes, all the worlds.
Where the gods, having attained immortality, soared up to the same abode.
This first-born of <s>Ṛta</s> (cosmic order) has encompassed all the worlds, has proclaimed [them].
The speaker in speech, dwelling in worlds—the bestower, the leader, the fierce <s>Agni</s>.
Around heaven and earth—this [first-born] of <s>Ṛta</s>, the wide-stretched thread, the star-haired one.
The god, guarding his divinity — who can discern his common bond?
By which this past, the world, and the future are all encompassed with immortality,
by which the sacrifice extends with its seven priests — may that mind of mine be of auspicious resolve (<s>śivasaṃkalpa</s>).
By which the wise and discerning ones perform rituals at the ceremonies,
that wondrous being (<s>yakṣa</s>), unprecedented, within all creatures — may that mind of mine be of auspicious resolve.
That which is insight (<s>prajñāna</s>), awareness, and steadfastness (<s>dhṛti</s>), the inner light, the immortal among beings,
without which nothing whatsoever is accomplished — may that mind of mine be of auspicious resolve.
That which, when awake, goes far — that divine [power], which likewise goes even when one sleeps,
the far-traveling one, the one light among lights — may that mind of mine be of auspicious resolve.
In which the <s>Ṛc</s>-verses, the <s>Sāman</s>-chants, and the <s>Yajus</s>-formulas are established like spokes in the hub of a wheel,
in which all thought of beings is woven — may that mind of mine be of auspicious resolve.
Like a skilled charioteer guiding horses with reins, [the mind] guides human beings as though [they were] swift steeds.
Established in the heart, unwearying, the swiftest — may that mind of mine be of auspicious resolve. [20]
That which here [constitutes] the six and three hundred of the body, the nine-naveled, primordial [parts] of the sacrifice,
the fifteen, the thirty-five, and whatever is beyond — may that mind of mine be of auspicious resolve.
Those that are five fives, a hundred, and a thousand, and a <s>niyuta</s> and a <s>nyarbuda</s>,
those sacrifice-minded bricks, that body — may that mind of mine be of auspicious resolve.
I know this great <s>Puruṣa</s>, of the sun's color, beyond darkness.
[...] the wise ones [...] — may that mind of mine be of auspicious resolve.
By which the wise and inspired ones perform actions, through speech, mind, and deed,
and living beings follow in concord — may that mind of mine be of auspicious resolve.
Those who are mind and heart, and those who are gods, who move about in manifold ways in the atmosphere,
who pervade hearing and sight — may that mind of mine be of auspicious resolve.
By which the mighty heaven, the earth, and the atmosphere — by which the mountains and the directions and quarters,
by which this whole moving world of beings is pervaded — may that mind of mine be of auspicious resolve.
By which all this world has come into being, those gods who are great and all-knowing (<s>Jātavedas</s>),
that, like <s>Agni</s>, is the one light born of austerity (<s>tapas</s>) — may that mind of mine be of auspicious resolve.
For you, O <s>Indra</s>, this honey is poured all around. [21]
Those [cows] whose udder has four openings, full of honey and ghee,
may they be milk-giving for us, many in the cowpen, dripping with ghee.
May the delightful one approach us, bringing nourishment (<s>ūrja</s>) and vigor (<s>ojas</s>).
Yielding inexhaustible milk — settle in my clan, that I may become the highest.
May the radiant great one drink the <s>soma</s>-honey. [22]
Do not fly away, O ram; return, O one of good sons.
For this woman of mine who desires a son, place an embryo that is male.
Just as this great earth, lying supine, received the embryo,
so place that embryo [in her], to be born in the tenth month.
In <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s most excellent form, in this woman, in [her] womb,
place a male son, to be born in the tenth month.
May the great aid of these three be [with us]. [23]
We invoke <s>Agni</s>, the radiant-faced one, with hymns for protection.
May he carry us beyond enemies.
Forth now, <s>Jātavedas</s>! [24]
(Adhyāya V, <s>Anukramaṇī</s>).

[<s>Anukramaṇī</s> index:] 'Saṃjñānam' — five [verses], <s>Kaśyapa</s>, <s>Saṃjñāna</s>, <s>Śamyu</s> the last, a blessing, <s>śakvarī</s> meter, everywhere. 'Nairhastyam' — a triplet, <s>Nirhastya</s>, enemy-destroying, army-routing, <s>ānuṣṭubha</s>, <s>bṛhatī</s> middle. 'Pra' — seven, <s>Kaśyapa</s>, <s>Jamadagni</s> the last, <s>Śamyu</s> the first, <s>Agni</s>-addressed, <s>gāyatrī</s>, the second and penultimate as blessing, <s>pāṅkta</s>, the third a syllable-praise in <s>anuṣṭubh</s>, fourth to <s>Soma</s>, fifth to <s>Sūrya</s>. 'Vidā' — ten pādas and five, <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, <s>Indra</s> or <s>Prajāpati</s>, <s>Aindra</s>, purificatory, <s>ānuṣṭubha</s>, with <s>purīṣapadas</s>, addressed to <s>Agni</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Pūṣan</s>, divine, <s>Vairāja</s>, second and fifth <s>uṣṇih</s>, fourth <s>nyaṅkusāriṇī</s>, seventh <s>purastādbṛhatī</s>, ninth and last <s>paṅktī</s>. 'Agniḥ' — eleven, deity indicated by the text, <s>yajus</s>-formulas. 'Vāyuḥ' — seven, deity proclaimed, <s>gāyatra</s>, sixth <s>śakvarī</s>, five <s>yājuṣa</s>-type. 'Hotā' — twelve, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> or invocation-hymns, the first an <s>āprī</s>, the rest deity indicated by the text, unspecified, deity of the self-sacrifice, otherwise proclaimed. 'Ajaid' — eleven, seventh and ninth <s>triṣṭubh</s>. 'Devam hotā' — eighteen. 'Hotā' — twelve. 'Idam' — triplet, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> and <s>Vāmadeva</s>, <s>Kuntāpa</s>, two <s>bṛhatīs</s> and <s>anuṣṭubh</s>. 'Vacyasvar' — ending in <s>anuṣṭubh</s>, a royal quatrain. 'Indraḥ' — ending in <s>paṅkti</s>. 'Yaḥ' — five. 'Yaṣṣaḍyat' — five, these two less, <s>Aitaśa</s> the sage, sixth and eighth <s>uṣṇih</s>, the last two-footed or <s>yajus</s>-formulas, four. 'Vitatau' — six, <s>ānuṣṭubha</s>. 'Ihettha' — quatrain, two-footed. 'Bhug' — single-footed <s>nicṛt</s>. 'Vi' — these <s>anuṣṭubh</s>. 'Ādityāḥ' — five, <s>jagatī</s>, <s>triṣṭubh</s>, above <s>bṛhatī</s>, fore-<s>bṛhatī</s>, two-footed or <s>yajus</s>. 'Tvam' — triplet, <s>ānuṣṭubha</s> however. 'Yad' — ten, dialogue of invoker and respondent, <s>Nākapṛtsu</s>, <s>jagatī</s> first, <s>jagatī</s> first.
<s>Uśanas</s> spoke concord (<s>saṃjñāna</s>), <s>Varuṇa</s> spoke concord,
<s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s> [spoke] concord, <s>Savitṛ</s> spoke concord.
Concord for us with our own people, concord with strangers,
O <s>Aśvins</s>, bestow concord upon us here.
What <s>Kakṣīvān</s>, son of the <s>Aṅgirases</s>, discovered as the means of winning over,
by that, may all the gods today make our beloved [come] together with us.
May your minds be in accord, may we think in accord in purpose.
That person who is disunited in mind — him we bring back together.
That [blessing] of <s>Śamyu</s> we choose: a path for the sacrifice, a path for the lord of sacrifice. May divine well-being be ours; may well-being be for humankind.
May the remedy rise upward; may there be well-being for the two-footed, well-being for the four-footed.
Enemy-routing, army-scattering — like an oblation around the path,
with that oblation we dry up the arms of the enemies.
<s>Indra</s> and <s>Pūṣan</s> have circled around their paths.
Of those burned by <s>Agni</s>, hidden by <s>Agni</s> — may <s>Indra</s> slay the best among them.
Bind upon these the despondency, like the timidity of a deer.
May [the weapon] pursue the enemies afar; may the cow come near. [2]
Forth, O lord of rites, O <s>Vasu</s>, O <s>Hotṛ</s>, most excellent, O resolute one,
for you the <s>Gāyatrī</s> is sung.
Desiring cattle, desiring food, desiring progeny — thus <s>Kaśyapa</s>,
praises the past and the future — the great <s>Brahman</s>, the one syllable; the manifold <s>Brahman</s>, the one syllable.
That syllable which all the gods, the makers of beings, worship,
they made <s>Jamadagni</s>, the great sage, its protector.
<s>Jamadagni</s> is nourished by meters increasing by four.
By partaking of King <s>Soma</s>, by the sacred power (<s>Brahman</s>) — auspicious for us be the directions and quarters, O valiant ones.
The unborn one [<s>Aja</s>] saw the radiance — bright, luminous, beyond, in the secret [cave].
That the seer <s>Kaśyapa</s> praises: the true <s>Brahman</s>, moving and unmoving; the eternal <s>Brahman</s>, moving and unmoving.
The triple lifespan of <s>Jamadagni</s>, the triple lifespan of <s>Kaśyapa</s>,
the triple lifespan of <s>Agastya</s>, that which is the triple lifespan of the gods — may that triple lifespan be ours.
That [blessing] of <s>Śamyu</s> we choose: a path for the sacrifice, a path for the lord of sacrifice. May divine well-being be ours; may well-being be for humankind.
May the remedy rise upward; may there be well-being for the two-footed, well-being for the four-footed. [3]
Know, O bounteous one, know the path; may you proclaim the directions.
Instruct, O lord of powers, of the many [blessings], O possessor of much.
With these aids, O perceptive one, make perceptive.
O <s>Indra</s>, for glory, to our [benefit] — thus indeed [does] <s>Śakra</s>.
For wealth, for prizes, O wielder of the thunderbolt, O mightiest, O thunderbolt-bearing one, you are urged on.
O most generous, thunderbolt-bearing one, urged on — come, drink, be delighted.
Know, for wealth and good heroism; become the lord of prizes, according to desire.
O most generous, thunderbolt-bearing one, urged on — he who is mightiest among heroes,
who is most generous among the bounteous, O discerning one, lead us.
<s>Indra</s> knows; him I praise — for <s>Śakra</s> is sovereign. [4]
Him we invoke for protection — the conqueror, the unconquered.
May he carry us beyond enemies; [he is] resolve, meter, cosmic order (<s>ṛta</s>), the great one.
We invoke <s>Indra</s> for the winning of wealth — the conqueror, the unconquered.
May he carry us beyond enemies; may he carry us beyond the hostile.
O stone-wielder, place us in the favor of the ancient [gods], O <s>Vasu</s>.
The fulfillment, O mightiest, is perpetual — for <s>Śakra</s> is sovereign.
Now you consider that new [praise], O lord of people, O slayer of <s>Vṛtra</s>.
Let us speak together among others — the hero who goes among the cattle, the friend, the gracious, the unwavering. [5]
Thus indeed, thus, O <s>Agni</s>! Thus indeed, thus, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>!
Thus indeed, thus, O <s>Indra</s>! Thus indeed, thus, O <s>Pūṣan</s>!
Thus indeed, thus, O gods!
Thus indeed <s>Śakra</s>, sovereign indeed <s>Śakra</s>, according to desire.
O iron one, to wrath, O wrathful ones! O one who approaches wrath, O wrathful ones! Come everywhere! [6]

children.translated_text: In his exhilaration, O singer, <s>Indra</s> was delighted by the <s>Soma</s>. In his exhilaration, O singer, <s>Indra</s> slew <s>Ahi</s> (the serpent). In his exhilaration, O singer, <s>Indra</s> slew <s>Vṛtra</s>. In his exhilaration—
<s>Vāyu</s>, the foremost, the sacrifice-lover, came together with the mind to the sacrifice.
Auspicious with his teams, with auspicious [mares].
The golden-wheeled two divine lords, for our protection.
<s>Vāyu</s> and <s>Indra</s>, of generous sacrifice.
The two wise kings, by their skill, in the home of <s>Dakṣa</s>.
The foe-consuming ones, in the seat.
The two divine priests, come with the sun-skinned chariot.
You two anoint the sacrifice with honey.
<s>Indra</s>, most delightful with hymns, lord of prizes among prizes.
The possessor of tawny [horses], the companion of the pressings.
We call all the gods, of beautiful form, to this sacrifice.
May the gods come to this sacrifice with divine thought.
Enjoying the seat at the rite, those who are the embodiments of the sacrifice—all, for <s>Soma</s>-drinking.
By speech, the great goddess <s>Vāc</s> (Speech), of beautiful form, at this sacrifice—
we call <s>Sarasvatī</s>. ||18
(<s>Praiṣa Adhyāya</s>—Chapter of Ritual Directives)

May the <s>Hotṛ</s> (priest) worship <s>Agni</s>, well-kindled with kindling, kindled at the navel of the earth, at the meeting-place of the good. May he go to the summit of heaven, to the seat of <s>Iḍā</s>. May the <s>Hotṛ</s> offer the oblation of ghee.
May the <s>Hotṛ</s> worship <s>Tanūnapāt</s> (protector of the body), the embryo of <s>Aditi</s>, the guardian of the world.
May the divine one today, with honey, anoint the god-going paths for the gods. May the <s>Hotṛ</s> offer the oblation of ghee.

May the <s>Hotṛ</s> worship <s>Narāśaṃsa</s> (praise of men), praised by men, the leader of men—may he be endowed with cows through vapā offerings, with heroes through powers, with chariots the foremost driver, with gold resplendent. May the <s>Hotṛ</s> offer the oblation of ghee.

May the <s>Hotṛ</s> worship <s>Agni</s>—praised by <s>Iḍā</s>. May the god invoke the god, the messenger, the carrier of oblations, the unerring one. May the god come to this sacrifice, to this divine invocation and protect [it]. May the <s>Hotṛ</s> offer the oblation of ghee.

May the <s>Hotṛ</s> worship the <s>Barhis</s> (sacred grass), well-spread, soft as wool. May it spread wide in this sacrifice. A good seat for the gods. May the <s>Vasus</s>, <s>Rudras</s>, and <s>Ādityas</s> sit upon it today as their beloved [seat]. May the <s>Hotṛ</s> offer the oblation of ghee.

May the <s>Hotṛ</s> worship the doors—high, opening upward, washing the coverings. May they open with their eloquent [openings]; may they spread in this sacrifice. Giving good passage, growing in <s>Ṛta</s> (cosmic order), may the <s>Hotṛ</s> offer the oblation of ghee.

May the <s>Hotṛ</s> worship <s>Uṣas</s> (Dawn) and <s>Naktā</s> (Night)—great, of beautiful form, making a womb for men as lords. Smiling with <s>Indra</s> and the gods, may they sit upon this <s>barhis</s>. May the <s>Hotṛ</s> offer the oblation of ghee.

May the <s>Hotṛ</s> worship the two divine <s>Hotṛs</s> (priests), delightful, the two <s>Potṛs</s> (purifiers), wise, far-seeing. May one today make the offering well-accomplished with food; may the other, well-praised, with nourishment and power—may they place this sacrifice in heaven among the gods.
May the <s>Hotṛ</s> worship the three goddesses, most skilled of the waters. May the waters weave this flawless work today.

May the <s>Hotṛ</s> worship <s>Tvaṣṭar</s>, most active, the distant seed-placer, possessor of all goods, holder of glory. Of many forms, emaciation-removing—may one be of good prosperity through prosperities, of good heroes through heroes. May the <s>Hotṛ</s> offer the oblation of ghee.

May the <s>Hotṛ</s> worship <s>Vanaspati</s> (lord of the forest). He has released the thoughts; the men enjoy the gentle one. May the <s>svadha</s> (self-offering) and the axe today, at the proper season, the divine one carry oblations to the gods. May the <s>Hotṛ</s> offer the oblation of ghee.

May the <s>Hotṛ</s> worship <s>Agni</s>—<s>svāhā</s> to the ghee's own offering, <s>svāhā</s> to the fat, <s>svāhā</s> to the drops, <s>svāhā</s> to the performed [offerings], <s>svāhā</s> to the well-spoken oblations. <s>Svāhā</s>—may the gods who drink ghee, enjoying, O <s>Agni</s>, partake of the ghee. May the <s>Hotṛ</s> offer.

<s>Agni</s> has won, has obtained prizes. The divine one [carried] the oblations for the gods. Impelled by the songs, fashioned by the hymns, the life of the sacrifice—go forth and convey the oblations to the gods, O <s>Hotṛ</s>.
May the <s>Hotṛ</s> worship <s>Agni</s>; may he enjoy the oblation of ghee. <s>Hotṛ</s>, offer.
May the <s>Hotṛ</s> worship <s>Soma</s>; may he enjoy the oblation of ghee. <s>Hotṛ</s>, offer.
May the <s>Hotṛ</s> worship <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s>; may the two enjoy the <s>vapā</s> (omentum) and fat of the goat offering. <s>Hotṛ</s>, offer.

May the <s>Hotṛ</s> worship <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s>; may the two enjoy the <s>puroḍāśa</s> (sacrificial cake) offering. <s>Hotṛ</s>, offer. May the <s>Hotṛ</s> worship <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s>; of the goat offering, may they partake today of the central fat extracted—

O <s>Vanaspati</s> (lord of the forest), [carry] the oblations to the gods, O golden-leaved one, since the earliest days, for your purpose. Binding [the victim] with the rope from right to left, carry [the offerings] on the straightest paths of <s>Ṛta</s> (cosmic order).

May the <s>Hotṛ</s> worship <s>Vanaspati</s> (Lord of the Forest). For with the most firmly bound, most excellent rope [he is tied]. Where are the beloved abodes of <s>Agni</s>'s oblation of ghee, where are the beloved abodes of <s>Soma</s>'s oblation of ghee, where are the beloved abodes of the goat-offering to <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s>, where are the beloved paths of <s>Vanaspati</s>, where are the beloved abodes of the ghee-drinking gods, where are the beloved abodes of <s>Agni</s> the <s>Hotṛ</s> — there, having praised him and having lauded him, he has released him, having made [him] as one who acts. May the divine <s>Vanaspati</s> thus enjoy the oblation. O <s>Hotṛ</s>, sacrifice!
O <s>Vanaspati</s>, bound with the firmly-tied rope, knowing the appointed times, carry the oblations to the gods, and proclaim the giver among the immortals.

May the <s>Hotṛ</s> worship <s>Agni Sviṣṭakṛt</s> (maker of good offerings). <s>Agni</s> has gone to the beloved abodes of <s>Agni</s>'s ghee-oblation, has gone to the beloved abodes of <s>Soma</s>'s ghee-oblation, has gone to the beloved abodes of the goat-offering to <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s>, has gone to the beloved paths of <s>Vanaspati</s>, has gone to the beloved abodes of the ghee-drinking gods. May he worship the beloved abodes of <s>Agni</s> the <s>Hotṛ</s>. May he worship his own greatness. May the sacrifice yield [wealth]; may he grant nourishment. May <s>Jātavedas</s> enjoy the oblation. O <s>Hotṛ</s>, sacrifice!

Today <s>Agni</s> has been chosen as the <s>Hotṛ</s> by this sacrificer — cooking the offerings, cooking the sacrificial cakes, taking the ghee for <s>Agni</s>, taking the ghee for <s>Soma</s>, binding the goat for <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s>. Well-established today, the divine Lord of the Forest became [the sacrificial post]. With ghee for <s>Agni</s>, with ghee for <s>Soma</s>, with a goat for <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s> — may the two strike it; cook the fat in return; may [the two] seize; may both be magnified — with sacrificial cakes. You, O <s>Ṛṣi</s>, descendant of <s>Ṛṣis</s>, grandson of <s>Ṛṣis</s>, today this sacrificer has chosen [you], having come from many assembled [people]. 'This one shall worship for me the excellent wealth among the gods.' Those gifts that the gods gave as divine gifts — instruct him in those and urge him. You are sent, O <s>Hotṛ</s>, commissioned for auspicious speech, for the human who speaks well; speak the well-spoken hymns. ||22

The divine sacrificial grass (<s>barhis</s>), well-divine, may it be with the gods; well-heroic with heroes. May it be turned at dawn, may it be spread at night. Surpassing others in wealth, may we rejoice. Of him who possesses <s>barhis</s> — may he come at the winning of wealth, at the granting of wealth. Sacrifice!

The divine doors — firm when closed, loose when opening, steady — at the invocation of the gods, may a calf or a newborn boy measure them. May no horse or dusty donkey approach them. May they open at the winning of wealth, at the granting of wealth. Sacrifice!

The divine <s>Uṣas</s> (Dawn) and <s>Naktā</s> (Night) — may the two invite [the gods] at this sacrifice that is offered. May the divine hosts now come forth. Well-pleased, well-established, may the two come at the winning of wealth, at the granting of wealth. Sacrifice!

The two divine female helpers (<s>Joṣṭrī</s>), placers of wealth — one of whom wards off sins and hatreds, the other brings excellent wealth to the sacrificer — at the winning of wealth, at the granting of wealth, may the two come. Sacrifice!

The two divine <s>Ūrjāhutī</s> (Nourishment-Oblations) — one brought nourishment and sustenance, the other [brought] communal eating and drinking. Sharing before and after — may we be [so]. That nourishment the two <s>Ūrjāhutī</s>, nourishing, have bestowed — at the winning of wealth, at the granting of wealth, may the two come. Sacrifice! ||23

The divine <s>Hotṛ</s> priests, <s>Potṛ</s> priests, <s>Neṣṭṛ</s> priests — slayers of evil speech — have brought wealth. At the winning of wealth, at the granting of wealth, may they come. Sacrifice!

The three divine goddesses — <s>Iḍā</s>, <s>Sarasvatī</s>, <s>Bhāratī</s> — <s>Bhāratī</s> touched the heaven with the <s>Ādityas</s>; <s>Sarasvatī</s> enveloped this sacrifice with the <s>Rudras</s>. Here may we rejoice at the communal feast with <s>Iḍā</s>, the possessor of wealth. At the winning of wealth, at the granting of wealth, may they come. Sacrifice!

The divine <s>Narāśaṃsa</s> (Praise of Men), three-headed, six-eyed — a hundred white-backed [horses] bear him, a thousand draw him forth. <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s> indeed [perform] his worthy <s>hotra</s> (invocation); <s>Bṛhaspati</s> [performs] the <s>stotra</s> (praise-chant); the <s>Aśvins</s> [perform] the <s>ādhvaryava</s> (Adhvaryu-function). At the winning of wealth, at the granting of wealth, may he come. Sacrifice!

The divine <s>Vanaspati</s> (Lord of the Forest), protector against rain, with ghee as his garment — he touched the heaven at the top, filled the atmosphere in the middle, and made firm the earth below. At the winning of wealth, at the granting of wealth, may he come. Sacrifice!

The divine sacrificial grass (<s>barhis</s>) — you are the laying-down of offerings, the unfallen support of the fallen, the firm supporter, the widely desirable, the glorious one. By means of this <s>barhis</s>, may we surpass all [other] grasses. At the winning of wealth, at the granting of wealth, may he come. Sacrifice!

The divine <s>Agni Sviṣṭakṛt</s> (maker of good offerings), bestower of fine wealth, inspiring, wise, of true thoughts, the worshipper, the <s>Hotṛ</s> of <s>Hotṛs</s>, giving life to the <s>Hotṛ</s> — O <s>Agni</s>, the gods whom you worshipped, whom you satisfied, who delighted in your <s>hotra</s> — that successful <s>hotra</s>, going to the gods, send forth the sacrifice to heaven among the gods. And O <s>Agni Sviṣṭakṛt</s>, you have become the <s>Hotṛ</s> — at the winning of wealth, at the granting of wealth, speak the word of homage (<s>namovāka</s>). Sacrifice!

May the <s>Hotṛ</s> worship <s>Indra</s>. May <s>Indra</s>, possessor of tawny horses, eat the grain; [may he eat] the barley-gruel accompanied by <s>Pūṣan</s>, the sifted grain accompanied by <s>Sarasvatī</s> and <s>Bhāratī</s>; [and] <s>Indra</s>'s cake. May <s>Indra</s>, delighting, come to the offered sacrificial cakes of the morning pressing. O <s>Hotṛ</s>, sacrifice! ||24

May the <s>Hotṛ</s> worship <s>Indra</s>. May <s>Indra</s>, possessor of tawny horses, eat the grain; [may he eat] the barley-gruel accompanied by <s>Pūṣan</s>, the sifted grain accompanied by <s>Sarasvatī</s> and <s>Bhāratī</s>; [and] <s>Indra</s>'s cake. May <s>Indra</s>, delighting, come to the offered sacrificial cakes of the midday pressing. O <s>Hotṛ</s>, sacrifice!

May the <s>Hotṛ</s> worship <s>Indra</s>. May <s>Indra</s>, possessor of tawny horses, eat the grain; [may he eat] the barley-gruel accompanied by <s>Pūṣan</s>, the sifted grain accompanied by <s>Sarasvatī</s> and <s>Bhāratī</s>; [and] <s>Indra</s>'s cake. May <s>Indra</s>, delighting, come to the offered sacrificial cakes of the third pressing. O <s>Hotṛ</s>, sacrifice!
May the <s>Hotṛ</s> worship <s>Agni</s>. May he enjoy the sacrificial cakes as the oblation. O <s>Hotṛ</s>, sacrifice!

May the <s>Hotṛ</s> worship <s>Vāyu</s>, who goes first, who has the foremost chariot, who drinks <s>Soma</s> first. May <s>Vāyu</s> thus come to this dwelling. May he enjoy, may he come, may he drink the <s>Soma</s>. O <s>Hotṛ</s>, sacrifice! ||25

May the <s>Hotṛ</s> worship <s>Indra</s> and <s>Vāyu</s>, the worthy ones, licking [the Soma], possessing cattle through cow-rich [offerings]; may the two be borne with heroism, with bright [Soma]. Their teams [are] foremost-going with cows; the two heroes — the whip before the horses — let them arrive here and be unyoked. May <s>Indra</s> and <s>Vāyu</s> thus enjoy, may they come, may they drink the <s>Soma</s>. O <s>Hotṛ</s>, sacrifice!

May the <s>Hotṛ</s> worship <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>, of excellent rule, consuming [enemies], never closing their eyes, watchful, vigilant — even from crooked paths knowing the way, with unblinding sight, meditating 'truth, truth.' May <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s> thus enjoy, may they come, may they drink the <s>Soma</s>. O <s>Hotṛ</s>, sacrifice!

May the <s>Hotṛ</s> worship the <s>Aśvins</s>, the <s>Nāsatyas</s>, blazing, moving with the <s>Rudras</s>. With the inner wheel bring hither good nourishment and sustenance, O excellent heroes; with the outer [wheel] ward off the hostile without anger. With the honey-whip, attend upon this sacrifice, O youthful ones. May the <s>Aśvins</s> thus enjoy, may they come, may they drink the <s>Soma</s>. O <s>Hotṛ</s>, sacrifice!

May the <s>Hotṛ</s> worship <s>Indra</s> at the morning pressing. May he come from near and from afar, from the broad atmosphere, from his own seat. These bright, honey-dripping [draughts] are offered to <s>Indra</s> as <s>Soma</s>. May he enjoy, may he come, may he drink the <s>Soma</s>. O <s>Hotṛ</s>, sacrifice!

May the <s>Hotṛ</s> worship <s>Indra</s> at the midday pressing — the exclusive portion — the eater, the drinker, the hearer, the one who comes at the call, the discerner of this prayer, the increaser of the pressing sacrificer. May he fill both flanks — both the <s>Vṛtra</s>-slaying and the great bounty. These bright <s>Manthin</s> (curd-mixed) [draughts] are offered to <s>Indra</s> as <s>Soma</s>. May he enjoy, may he come, may he drink the <s>Soma</s>. O <s>Hotṛ</s>, sacrifice! ||26

May the <s>Hotṛ</s> worship <s>Indra</s> at the third pressing, accompanied by the <s>Ṛbhus</s>, <s>Vibhu</s>, <s>Vāja</s>, <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, and the <s>Viśvedevas</s>. His intoxications from the morning pressing have come together, and those of the midday, and those of the evening. Of those assembled [draughts], like a bull plunging in — be virile, be strong! Come with both arms, with the two tawny horses; puffing out your lips, O <s>Ṛjīṣin</s> (drinker of the residue) — these strong <s>Soma</s> draughts mixed with curds are offered to <s>Indra</s>. May he enjoy, may he come, may he drink the <s>Soma</s>. O <s>Hotṛ</s>, sacrifice!

May the <s>Hotṛ</s> worship <s>Indra</s> accompanied by the <s>Maruts</s>. May <s>Indra</s> accompanied by the <s>Maruts</s> enjoy, may he come, may he drink the <s>Soma</s>. O <s>Hotṛ</s>, sacrifice!

May the <s>Hotṛ</s> worship the <s>Ādityas</s>, the dear ones, of dear abodes, of dear vows, lords of the great firmament, overseers of the broad atmosphere. He has proclaimed the <s>Āditya</s>-hood. May he do so for this pressing sacrificer. May the <s>Ādityas</s> thus enjoy, may they be gladdened, may they come, may they drink, may they delight in the <s>Soma</s>. O <s>Hotṛ</s>, sacrifice!

May the <s>Hotṛ</s> worship the divine <s>Savitṛ</s>. May he send away disease, may he send away evil speech; may he impel what is well-impelled. May he do so for this pressing sacrificer. May the divine <s>Savitṛ</s> thus enjoy, may he be gladdened, may he come, may he drink the <s>Soma</s>. O <s>Hotṛ</s>, sacrifice!

Today <s>Agni</s> has been chosen as the <s>Hotṛ</s> by this pressing sacrificer — cooking the offerings, cooking the sacrificial cakes, taking the ghee for <s>Agni</s>, taking the ghee for <s>Soma</s>, binding the goat for <s>Agni</s>, pressing <s>Soma</s> for <s>Indra</s>, roasting the grain for the two tawny horses. Well-established today, the divine Lord of the Forest became [the sacrificial post]. With ghee for <s>Agni</s>, with ghee for <s>Soma</s>, with a goat for <s>Agni</s>, with <s>Soma</s> for <s>Indra</s>, with grain for the two tawny horses — may the two strike; cook the fat in return; may he seize; may he be magnified — with sacrificial cakes. <s>Indra</s> drank the <s>Soma</s> mixed with cow's [milk], mixed with barley, strong at the end, rich in the middle. The intoxications rose up; he roared in ecstasy; he was magnified with praises. You, O <s>Ṛṣi</s>, descendant of <s>Ṛṣis</s>, grandson of <s>Ṛṣis</s> — today this pressing sacrificer has chosen [you], having come from many assembled [people]. 'This one shall worship for me the excellent wealth among the gods.' Those gifts that the gods gave as divine gifts — instruct him in those and urge him. You are sent, O <s>Hotṛ</s>, commissioned for auspicious speech, for the human who speaks well; speak the well-spoken hymns. ||27

The grain of the <s>Soma</s> draughts — from <s>Indra</s> indeed both eat and drink. The two tawny horses bound [to you] — may they smell the grain along with the residue (<s>ṛjīṣa</s>). Pour upon the chariot, O [thou] of the people! When [your wives] asked you, 'Where did you become intoxicated?' — [the answer is:] 'At the house of this pressing sacrificer.' What have you granted him? Good heroism. [You are] the manager of the sacrifice's surplus. Whatever he desired, that very thing came to be. O <s>Hotṛ</s>, sacrifice!

Here indeed become intoxicated, O generous <s>Indra</s>! Tomorrow's [pressing will be] accompanied by the <s>Vasus</s>, the <s>Rudras</s>, the <s>Ādityas</s>, the <s>Ṛbhus</s>, <s>Vibhu</s>, <s>Vāja</s>, <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, and the <s>Viśvedevas</s>. For tomorrow's pressing, proclaim <s>Agni</s> for <s>Indra</s>, for <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>, for <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>, for the <s>Vasus</s>, the <s>Rudras</s>, the <s>Ādityas</s>, all the gods, for the <s>Brahman</s>-priests, those devoted to <s>Soma</s>, those who drink <s>Soma</s>. O <s>Brahman</s> priest, grant speech!

May the <s>Hotṛ</s> worship the <s>Aśvins</s> with the <s>Soma</s> draughts of the day-long [rites]. Thrice may the two come on their course, thrice daily may the two be honored, and a fourth time too, O <s>Nāsatyas</s>, for the prize-seeking [sacrificer], O gods! Together with <s>Agni</s>, the red horse, ghee-dripping; together with <s>Uṣas</s> (Dawn), with the reddish [horses]; together with <s>Sūrya</s> (Sun), with the dappled [horses]; in harmony, the two <s>Aśvins</s>, with their jaws. May the <s>Aśvins</s> thus enjoy, may they be gladdened, may they come, may they drink the <s>Soma</s>. O <s>Hotṛ</s>, sacrifice! ||28
May the <s>Hotṛ</s> worship <s>Indra</s> from the <s>Hotra</s> (invocation office), together with Heaven and Earth. May he drink the <s>Soma</s> in due season. O <s>Hotṛ</s>, sacrifice!

May the <s>Hotṛ</s> worship the <s>Maruts</s> from the <s>Potra</s> (Potṛ's office), the well-praising ones, of beautiful chant. May they drink the <s>Soma</s> in due season. O <s>Potṛ</s>, sacrifice!

May the <s>Hotṛ</s> worship the pressing-stones; from the <s>Neṣṭṛ's</s> [cup], <s>Tvaṣṭar</s> of good births, together with the wives of the gods, may he drink the <s>Soma</s> at the season. <s>Neṣṭṛ</s>, offer.
May the <s>Hotṛ</s> worship <s>Agni</s>; from the <s>Āgnīdhra's</s> [cup], may he drink the <s>Soma</s> at the season. <s>Āgnīdhra</s>, offer.
May the <s>Hotṛ</s> worship <s>Indra</s>, the <s>Brahman</s> (priest); from the <s>Brahman's</s> [cup], may he drink the <s>Soma</s> at the season. <s>Brahman</s>, offer.
May the <s>Hotṛ</s> worship <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>, the directors; from the director's [cup], may the two drink the <s>Soma</s> at the season. Director, offer. ||29
May the <s>Hotṛ</s> worship the god <s>Draviṇodas</s> (wealth-giver); from the <s>Hotṛ's</s> [cup], may he drink the <s>Soma</s> at the seasons. <s>Hotṛ</s>, offer.
May the <s>Hotṛ</s> worship the god <s>Draviṇodas</s>; from the <s>Potṛ's</s> [cup], may he drink the <s>Soma</s> at the seasons. <s>Potṛ</s>, offer.
May the <s>Hotṛ</s> worship the god <s>Draviṇodas</s>; from the <s>Neṣṭṛ's</s> [cup], may he drink the <s>Soma</s> at the seasons. <s>Neṣṭṛ</s>, offer.

May the <s>Hotṛ</s> worship the god <s>Draviṇodas</s>; from the <s>Hotṛ's</s> [cup], from the <s>Potṛ's</s> [cup], from the <s>Neṣṭṛ's</s> [cup]—the fourth cup, unhurt, immortal, <s>Indra's</s> draught—may the god <s>Draviṇodas</s> drink. The gifts of <s>Draviṇodas</s>—
May the <s>Hotṛ</s> worship the <s>Aśvins</s>, the two <s>Adhvaryus</s> (priests); from the <s>Adhvaryu's</s> [cup], may the two drink the <s>Soma</s> at the season. <s>Adhvaryus</s>, offer.
May the <s>Hotṛ</s> worship <s>Agni</s> the householder, from the household fire. May he be a good householder. O <s>Agni</s>, may the one who presses [Soma] and sacrifices be a good householder—
People, hear this: <s>Narāśaṃsa</s> (praise of men) shall be lauded.
Sixty thousand and ninety [cows] of the <s>Kaurava</s>—we receive [them] among the tawny rams.
He whose draft-animals are camels, with brides, twice twelve.
The height of the chariot reaches to heaven, touching the sky.
For this [purpose] we praise—a hundred gold necklaces, ten garlands.
Three hundred horses, ten thousand cows. ||31
Sing, O <s>Rebha</s> (singer), sing—like a bird on a ripe tree.
Your tongue darts out like a razor on a broad [surface].
The <s>Rebhas</s> (singers) move with thought, freely, like cows.
Their sons are unbound; and those who rejoice attend upon [them].
O <s>Rebha</s>, bring forth the thought that finds cows, that finds treasure.
Hear this speech [directed] to the gods; like an arrow, O hero, [hear] the archer. ||32
Of the king, ruler of all peoples, who is a god surpassing mortals,
the well-praised hymn of <s>Vaiśvānara</s>—press out [Soma] for <s>Parikṣit</s>.
<s>Parikṣit</s> has made peace for us; that seat [is] the shelter.
Making generous gifts, the <s>Kauravya</s> (descendant of Kuru), the husband, speaks with his wife:
'Which shall I bring you—curd, mixed drink, or strained [liquor]?'
The wife asks the husband in the kingdom of King <s>Parikṣit</s>.
Like the sun, it springs forth; the ripe barley [fills] the opening of the path.
That people prospers in the kingdom of King <s>Parikṣit</s>. ||33
<s>Indra</s> awakened the singer: 'Rise up, go about, wandering.'
'My fierce fame [spreads]; may every patron fulfill [your needs].'
'Here, O cows, be born; here, horses; here, men.'
'Here let the hero of a thousand gifts, the protector, sit down.'
'May these cows of yours not perish, O <s>Indra</s>; may their cowkeeper not perish.'
'May no hostile person [harm] them, O <s>Indra</s>; may no thief have power [over them].'
We come to you, O men, with a well-spoken word, with a blessed word.
Accept our songs with pleasure; may we never come to harm. ||34
He who is fit for the assembly, for the council, who presses [Soma] and sacrifices—such a man—
the sun [and] the foe-consuming bowl—the gods arranged that first.
He who refuses a kinswoman, who seeks to deceive his friends—
the eldest who is without understanding—they say he goes downward.
When the son of a noble man becomes bold,
the sage spoke upward; the <s>Gandharva</s> [spoke] the desired word.
He who is a miserly <s>Paṇi</s>, ungenerous, and he who is wealthy but does not give—
I have heard from the eternal wise ones: 'That [person goes] away [from prosperity].'
And those who did not sacrifice to the gods, and those who took away [the offerings]—
like the sun going to heaven, the generous ones shine. ||35
He whose eyes are not anointed, who has no ornaments, no gold—
the non-brahmin, the non-brahmin's son—they are measured in such [low] eons.
He whose eyes are anointed, well-adorned, with beautiful ornaments, with beautiful gold—
the good brahmin, the brahmin's son—they are measured in such [noble] eons.
Without watering-places, and the market-town; wealthy, [yet] without activity; and the niggard—
a maiden unsuitable for marriage, O fair one—they are measured in such eons.
With good watering-places, and the market-town; wealthy, with great activity; and the generous—
a maiden suitable for marriage, O fair one—they are measured in such eons.
Both the rejected wife and the chief queen; and through good fortune, one goes to battle—
the father-in-law's horse-trainer—they are measured in such eons.
Both the desired wife and the great-jeweled one; and [one goes] to battle—
without a father-in-law's horse-trainer—they are measured in such eons. ||36
When, O <s>Indra</s>, you entered the ten kings' human [battle],
<s>Virūpa</s> was [present] for all—resembling the die, he deceives.
You, O bounteous one, turned around the crooked dice.
You [opened] the jaws of <s>Rauhiṇa</s>; you split the head of <s>Vṛtra</s>.
He who set apart the mountains, who entered the waters—
who slew <s>Vṛtra</s>, O <s>Vṛtra</s>-slayer—salutation be to you, O <s>Indra</s>.
I called to the chief [horse], swift, <s>Uccaiḥśravas</s>, of the two tawny [steeds],
'Hail to the horse-conquering [steed]! Bring <s>Indra's</s> chariot here.'
When the white <s>Uccaiḥśravas</s> is yoked to the right of the two tawny ones,
the foremost horse of the gods, carrying <s>Indra</s>, he is glorified. ||37
These mares swim forth, upstream, against the current.
Among them, one is tawny-hued. 'O tawny-hued one, what do you desire?'
'A good son, golden.' 'Where have you cast him away?'
'Where those three <s>Śiṃśapā</s> trees [stand], around [which] three serpents—'
'Sit blowing a horn.' 'This one, carry, I have carried.'
'He is thus indeed, he is even so. Fellow with you, fellow with me.'
'He owns cows, he is a cow-owner indeed. O man, you seek to deceive [for] the great [prize].'
'Balbab, and so.' 'Balbab, and so.'
'The goat-crow-quail [sound].' 'The horse's tail, the cow's hoof.'
'The hairy one, the hawk-like, the deer-like'—healthy, the small tongue. ||38
'Who, O mother, [knows] the pestle of the mortar?' 'Who [knows] the milk of the white [cow]?'
'Who [knows] the milk of the black [cow]?' 'Ask this, ask "where."'
'Where is the ripe [fruit]—ask.' Those who come with dogs, with humps—
'Water-dwellers, hump-people.' 'The stingy one, the mind-dweller.'
'God-given, to be honored.' 'The grinding-woman grinds the oblation.'
'The bubble churns forth.' 'The stalk rises up.'
'<s>Irā</s> (refreshment) and <s>Indra</s> delighted.' 'Going, going'—thus.
'And so, going,' they say. 'And so, he became greater.'
'This peg, the small pin'—it bends, it breaks apart. ||39
'Its un-breaking [remedy]—' <s>Varuṇa</s> goes with the tawny ones.
A hundred tawny ones with reins, a hundred golden whips.
A hundred golden chariots. The dark one, the whirler.
With the driving-goad, the sharpener. With the hoof he carries the fat one.
With the rump he dances about. 'Give this to me'—thus.
'Those trees stand together.' '<s>Pākavali</s>, <s>Śakavali</s>.'
'The <s>Aśvattha</s>, the <s>Khadira</s>, the <s>Dhava</s>.' 'The wheel lies supreme.'
'Like a wicked slain man.' 'I milked the first milk.'
'Two skins of two elephants.' 'And a half of another's.'
'Then one gourd.' 'A gourd buried in the ground.' ||40
'A pot buried in the ground.' 'The wind churns that up.'
'I shall make a nest,' he says. 'The fierce, strung [bow].'
'Not the un-strung [bow].' 'Who shall scratch their drum?'
'Who shall beat their <s>dundubhi</s> (drum)?' 'When he beats, how does he beat?'
'He beats a <s>dailī</s> (small drum)—how does he beat it? Around and around, again and again.' ||41
Two threads are stretched out—the man squeezes them together.
'Not as you think, O maiden, is it truly so.'
'Your mother's two threads—the girdle apart from a man.'
'Not as you think, O maiden, is it truly so.'
'Grasping two little ears, you draw out the middle.'
'Not as you think, O maiden, is it truly so.'
'To one lying face-up, while standing, you push in.'
'Not as you think, O maiden, is it truly so.'
'In the smooth, into the smooth [hole], you push in smoothly.'
'Not as you think, O maiden, is it truly so.'
'The smooth [thing] falls down, into the hairy pool.'
'Not as you think, O maiden, is it truly so.' ||42
Here, thus, east, west, north, south—the crooked one cried out.
Here, thus, east, west, north, south—the calves sit spraying.
Here, thus, east, west, north, south—the pot-cooker dissolves.
Here, thus, east, west, north, south—the scorpion-tail dissolves.
'Bhuk!'—having arrived. 'Śar!'—having stood.
'Phal!'—having departed.
These gods cried out: 'O <s>Adhvaryu</s>, proceed quickly!'
'The good praise is of cows indeed—beyond the great annoyances.' ||43
The <s>Ādityas</s>, O singer, brought the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (sacrificial fee) for the <s>Aṅgiras</s> [sages].
That, O singer, they did not accept back; but that, O singer, they did accept back.
That, O singer, they did not seize back; but that, O singer, they did seize back.
Ah, being a leader, [he finds] unintelligent [followers]; being born a leader, without foregoers.
And the white one, swift-flying; and by feet, the fastest.
And he carries the swiftly-going one.
The <s>Ādityas</s>, <s>Rudras</s>, and <s>Vasus</s> [say]: 'Accept this gift, O <s>Aṅgiras</s>.'
'This gift, great and broad—may the gods grant the best.'
'May that be of good understanding for you; may it be yours day after day.'
'Accept it indeed.' ||44
You, O <s>Indra</s>, in your protection, bring the oblation from the distant ones.
For the sage who praises, [bring] wealth; you carry [them] straight to glory.
You, O <s>Indra</s>, for the pigeon with broken wing, stumbling—
you cracked open the ripe millet; you made much shelter for him.
The <s>Āraṅgara</s> bird chatters, bound three ways, going about, iron-like.
It praises refreshment indeed, and rejects the lack of refreshment. ||45
When from her narrow opening, a broad thick [thing] rose up—
her two testicle-like [parts] quivered, like two fish on a cow's hoof.
When with a thick membrane she struck the two small testicle-like [parts]—
the two separated, like two donkeys on the sand.
When the little, very little one ripens like a <s>Karkandhuka</s> berry,
like a spring twig, being bent, she bends down.
When the gods found the gourd-like fish entering—
O woman, it is seen between your thighs, like the portion of truth's eye. ||46
The <s>Mahānagnī</s> (great naked woman) calls out: 'Tomorrow, the lodged member.'
'Of such a fruit-tree, may we have winnowing-basket after winnowing-basket.'
The <s>Mahānagnī</s>, unhumbled, crying out, sat down at home.
'Capable of desire, the fly, the thigh raised up.'
The <s>Mahānagnī</s>, stepping over the mortar, said:
'Just as they pound you, O tree, so [may they pound] me.'
The <s>Mahānagnī</s> runs around the rooster with a stick.
'We do not know this sharpener—by the head it becomes a receptacle.'
The <s>Mahānagnī</s>, the great-rumped one, runs after the running one.
Guard these cows of his; enjoy me, eat the rice.
Great indeed is the auspicious <s>bilva</s> tree; great is the ripe <s>udumbara</s> tree.
The great one overpowers at the knee; great is the good churning.
O men, set up the penis, the copulation; urge on, dig, for the winning of prizes.
The <s>Niṣṭigrya</s> [women] move the son forth, for aids — [bring] <s>Indra</s>, along with pressure, here for <s>soma</s>-drinking.
When the broad [vessels], like rust-removing pans, went forth,
the enemies of <s>Indra</s> are slain — all the bubble-like, perishing ones.
This has been made for <s>Dadhikrāvan</s>, the victorious, the prize-winning horse.
May he make our mouths fragrant; may he extend our lifespans. [47]
(<s>Saṃhitā Āraṇya</s>)
: Having risen, I hold the radiance; that I hold within myself. May vital power follow me; in me be prosperity (<s>Śrī</s>), in me be fame.

: I rise with the breath of all, with strength — may blessing rise after me; may the deities follow me. [With] uninjured sight, vigorous mind — <s>Sūrya</s>, the best of luminaries — O consecration (<s>Dīkṣā</s>), do not harm me.
: That divine eye, bright and radiant, has risen. May we see a hundred autumns; may we live a hundred autumns.

At the end of a hymn, [I perform the ritual] in fire, in the forest, or in water.
What has been studied with grass-blades — that has been mastered; become grass-blades, become!
Of wells, ponds, and reservoirs — go to the ocean, <s>svāhā</s>! Go to fire, <s>svāhā</s>!
O lord of all, of various forms and eyes, of all forms, O ever-auspicious <s>Sadāśiva</s>,
be our refuge, O lord of beings, O compassionate <s>Śaṃkara</s>,
O <s>Hara</s>, O <s>Śambhu</s>, O great god (<s>Mahādeva</s>), O lord of all, O beloved of the immortals,
O <s>Śiva</s>, O <s>Śaṃkara</s>, O universal Self (<s>Sarvātman</s>), O blue-throated one (<s>Nīlakaṇṭha</s>), homage to you!
To the conqueror of death (<s>Mṛtyuṃjaya</s>), to <s>Rudra</s>, to the blue-throated one, to <s>Śambhu</s>,
to the lord of immortality, to <s>Śarva</s>, to the glorious <s>Mahādeva</s> — homage to you!
He who recites these names of <s>Śiva</s> regularly, even once,
for him there is no fear of death, nor any sin, disease, or the like.
O <s>Yajñeśa</s>, <s>Acyuta</s>, <s>Govinda</s>, <s>Mādhava</s>, <s>Ananta</s>, <s>Keśava</s>,
O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>, <s>Vāsudeva</s> — homage to you!
To <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, to the lord of the <s>gopīs</s> (<s>Gopīnātha</s>), to the discus-bearer, to the foe of the <s>asuras</s>,
to the lord of immortality, to the cowherd (<s>Gopā</s>), to <s>Govinda</s> — homage, homage!
These names of <s>Ananta</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) one should always recite at the end of a <s>maṇḍala</s>.
What has been studied with grass-blades — that has been mastered; become grass-blades, become!
Of wells, ponds, and reservoirs — go to the ocean, <s>svāhā</s>!
At the end of a hymn, [cast] the grass-blades into fire.
Where the white and dark rivers meet, there those who have bathed fly up to heaven.
Those wise ones who release their bodies — those people partake of immortality.
Some attain heaven with oblations; some press <s>soma</s> at the pressings.
Exulting in powers and with gifts — may we not fall crookedly into the netherworld (<s>naraka</s>).
With the membrane of snow, O dwelling (<s>śālā</s>), we cover you around.
And may the pool be for us; may <s>Agni</s> grant the remedy.
May the cool pool be for us; may <s>Agni</s> grant the remedy.
He who kindled fire nearby — the irresistible child came.
My heart aches for her who has no born son, whose wings are unfeathered.
Go, O <s>Jātavedas</s>, through the vast forest, the wide space, for desire.
Protect me and [my] sons; [I have] taken refuge in you.
O tawny-eyed, red-necked, dark-colored one — homage to you!
Cast down our enemies utterly, like the waves of the ocean.
May <s>Indra</s> grant sovereignty; may he consecrate with <s>Varuṇa</s>'s [authority].
May the enemies go to destruction; may you [have] victory, by the power of <s>Brahman</s>.
The matted-haired one of the <s>Kalpa</s>, the all-consuming fire, the directly visible deity,
and <s>Varuṇa</s> — I command first: may he protect my sons! May he protect my sons! Oṃ namaḥ.
Live a full hundred years and more; drink, eat, and rejoice.
And protect the afflicted, the twice-born, the offspring, and the cattle.
As long as the sun blazes, as long as the moon shines,
as long as the wind blows — so long live, conquering, ever conquering!
By whatever means one sustains one's family,
he who lives for the benefit of others — he truly lives.
This is the <s>Vaiśvānarī</s> [fire] — homage to you, O all gods!
No fear of thieves, no fear of serpents, no fear of tigers, no fear of death.
For whom there is no untimely death, nor [any] death at all — he obtains everything; he conquers everything.
